A_designs.topic: Topic A: rotary kiln designs and operating data for plastic pyrolysis (and related mixed plastic, MSW/RDF, tyre and biomass kilns), from lab to industrial scale, ending in a recommended continuous, indirectly heated reference case for mixed polyolefin flakes

findings.parameter: Kodera bench kiln (AIST), plastic, continuous: geometry
findings.value: retort OD 216 mm x length 1000 mm; narrowed end flanges 110 mm ID that keep sand/additives inside
findings.context: Bench, externally heated rotary kiln; PP and PP/PET laminate; fuel-gas route
findings.source: Kodera Y., Yamamoto T., Ishikawa E. (2021) Energy- and economic-balance estimation of pyrolysis plant for fuel-gas production from plastic waste based on bench-scale plant operations. Fuel Communications 7:100016
findings.evidence: Search-engine extraction of the OA article: 'outer diameter of 216 mm and a length of 1000 mm, with narrowed end flanges (110 mm inner diameter) to hold sand or additives in place'. A second search could not re-confirm the flange detail.

findings.parameter: Kodera bench kiln: operating point
findings.value: Feed 1–3.1 kg/h (abstract: '1 to 3-kg/h'; scale-up based on 2 kg/h runs); 5 kg silica sand held in the retort as heating medium; N2 purge; kiln heated to 650 °C; MgO + steam variant also run
findings.context: PP and PP/PET laminates
findings.source: Kodera et al. 2021, Fuel Communications 7:100016
findings.evidence: Highlights/abstract: 'gaseous hydrocarbon yields of 54.7–69.1 wt% at 650 °C ... 1–3.1 kg/h feeding rate'; methods snippet: 'silica sand (5 kg) ... Nitrogen gas was purged ... rotary kiln was heated to 650 °C'. Rotation speed and N2 flow not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Kodera: gas yield vs temperature, PP in rotary kiln
findings.value: 58.5 / 64.4 / 66.1 wt% gas at 650 / 700 / 750 °C; 64.2 wt% gas in a PP run at 1.007 kg/h; overall 54.7–69.1 wt% gaseous HC at 650 °C
findings.context: Externally heated bench kiln with a sand bed; long vapour residence, high T; fuel-gas oriented
findings.source: Kodera et al. 2021 (values quoted in a citing article and in the abstract)
findings.evidence: 'reactions were performed at temperatures 650, 700, and 750 °C using a rotary kiln, and the gas yields obtained equaled 58.5, 64.4, and 66.1 wt%'

findings.parameter: Kodera: 200 kg/h scale-up kiln design (plastic)
findings.value: Kiln OD 2.04 m and length 4.88 m. Wall layers: retort 0.01 m, heating-gas chamber 0.10 m, insulation shell 0.15 m, which gives a DERIVED retort ID of about 1.52 m. Surface heat loss E_R = 49.9 MJ/h (about 13.9 kW). Annual LHV output: pyrolysis gas 3.86e7 MJ/y, oil 4.28e6 MJ/y; 1.49e7 MJ/y consumed by the process. A citing paper gives about 60 kW of heating power for the 200 kg/h case.
findings.context: Simulated self-supplied commercial plant, externally heated by combustion of its own pyrolysis gas
findings.source: Kodera et al. 2021, Fuel Communications 7:100016
findings.evidence: Snippet: 'outer diameter of the rotary kiln was 2.04 m and the length was 4.88 m. Then, the heat emission ... E_R, was estimated as 49.9 MJ/h'. Operating hours not retrieved, so the annual figures cannot be converted to kW reliably. The 60 kW figure is secondary.

findings.parameter: Dalian (A. Li group) lab rotary kiln with solid heat carrier: optimum loading and oil yield
findings.value: Optimum heat-carrier loading (filling ratio) 15% for oil; maximum oil 57.6 wt% at 625 °C, with oil cracking to light gases above that; oils contain 71.8–89.1% gasoline-range HC; more heat carrier raises oil and char and lowers gas
findings.context: PE, PP, PS and a simulated mixed plastic (SMP); externally heated lab kiln
findings.source: Zhang Y., Ji G., Chen et al., Li A. (2020) Liquid oils produced from pyrolysis of plastic wastes with heat carrier in rotary kiln. Fuel Processing Technology 206:106455
findings.evidence: 'increasing pyrolysis temperature up to 625 °C promoted the production of pyrolysis-oil and its yield reached 57.6 wt%'; '15% is the optimal heat carrier loading'. Kiln dimensions and heat-carrier material/size not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Dalian heat-carrier kiln: rotation and filling tested; contact heat transfer
findings.value: Rotation 1, 3 and 6 rpm; filling 10, 15 and 20%. Measured contact heat-transfer coefficients matched only one of four literature models.
findings.context: Same group, heat-carrier plastic pyrolysis
findings.source: ResearchGate record of Zhang et al. 2020 (FPT 206:106455), search summary
findings.evidence: Search summary of the ResearchGate page. The exact wording was not visible.

findings.parameter: Dalian kiln: energy/exergy efficiency and self-heating
findings.value: SMP pyrolysis: exergy efficiency 60.9–67.3%, energy efficiency 59.4–66.0% (one summary instead gives 59.4–66.0% as total exergy efficiency). Self-heating by burning recycled gas and char is achievable for PE at 15% heat-carrier loading and for SMP at 20%. At 15% filling, carbon conversion to oil from SMP peaks at 62.8 wt%.
findings.context: Lab rotary kiln with heat carrier
findings.source: Zhang Y., Ji G., Ma C., Chen X., Wang Y., Wang W., Li A. (2020) Exergy and energy analysis of pyrolysis of plastic wastes in rotary kiln with heat carrier. Process Safety and Environmental Protection 142:203–211
findings.evidence: Abstract/highlights. The two summaries conflict on which number is exergy and which is energy.

findings.parameter: Quartz-sand heat carrier in a plastic kiln: DEM results
findings.value: Loading 5–15%. At 5% the bed slips as a whole and mean particle angular velocity is about one order of magnitude lower. More carrier gives faster plastic heating, shorter volatile retention, more oil and char, and less gas.
findings.context: EDEM simulation of a plastic-pyrolysis rotary kiln
findings.source: The simulation of particle movement and heat transfer in rotary kiln for plastic waste pyrolysis. Chinese Science Bulletin (Kexue Tongbao) 2020, doi 10.1360/TB-2020-0765
findings.evidence: Abstract summary via search

findings.parameter: HDPE in a rotary kiln (batch experiments + CFD-DEM): gas yield vs T
findings.value: Gas yield rises from 32.55% to 56.33% between 480 and 600 °C; oil and wax yields fall (secondary cracking)
findings.context: HDPE, rotary kiln, batch experiments used to validate CFD-DEM (particle motion, gas-solid heat transfer, multi-step kinetics)
findings.source: Probably Liu C., Dai S., Li A. (2026) CFD–DEM coupled simulation and experimental study of polyethylene pyrolysis in a rotary kiln. J. Environ. Chem. Eng. 14(3):122678 (attribution not fully confirmed)
findings.evidence: Snippet: 'batch experiments at 480–600 °C ... raising gas yield from 32.55% to 56.33% while oil and wax yields decreased'. The validation error is truncated in the snippet.

findings.parameter: Rotation-speed effect on plastic pyrolysis products (externally heated kiln, PP and PE)
findings.value: Optimum 4 r/min for pyrolytic-oil yield. Within a certain speed range, raising speed shifts heavy oil to light oil. PE gas composition is sensitive to speed and PP gas is not. Char heating value rises by up to 31.5% (PP) and 116.1% (PE).
findings.context: Lab or pilot externally heated rotary kiln (dimensions unknown)
findings.source: Influence of rotating speed on pyrolysis products of waste plastics in rotary kiln (Chinese journal, authors not retrieved)
findings.evidence: 'the rotating speed should be set at 4r/min to enhance the productive rate of pyrolytic oil'

findings.parameter: Wall-to-waste overall heat-transfer coefficient k_m-w (externally heated waste kiln incl. plastic)
findings.value: 38.6 W/m2K (no lifters) rising to 45.3 W/m2K with six 200 mm lifters at 2.7 rpm, and to 50.1 W/m2K at 4.0 rpm. About +10% when lifter height / waste-layer thickness > 0.45 or lifter-to-interface arc ratio > 1. Lifter number matters most during plastic pyrolysis; lifter height matters most during water evaporation.
findings.context: Externally heated rotary kiln for waste pyrolysis; dimensionless correlation fitted for 100–500 °C
findings.source: Suzuki T. et al. (2008) Improvements in Pyrolysis of Wastes in an Externally Heated Rotary Kiln (Experimental Study on Heat Transfer Enhancement). J. Thermal Science and Technology 3(3):532–539, doi 10.1299/jtst.3.532
findings.evidence: Abstract quotes given in the evidence. Kiln diameter not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Indirectly heated kiln, medical waste (contains plastics): heat-transfer coefficient vs fill, rpm and heat-source T
findings.value: h falls from 182.2 to 153.5 W/m2K as filling ratio rises from 11.3% to 37.5%, with a slower decline above 22.5%. h rises from 169.2 to 186.5 W/m2K as speed rises from 0.5 to 3 rpm. A 1.5 rpm threshold changes the solids transport regime. Heat source 700–850 °C; at 750–850 °C, time to complete pyrolysis falls from about 5.04 h to 2.28 h. Overall reported range about 150–240 W/m2K.
findings.context: Batch, indirectly heated rotary kiln, mixed medical waste
findings.source: Heat transfer and parameter optimization for medical waste pyrolysis in an indirectly heated rotary kiln. Waste Management 2025, doi 10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115093
findings.evidence: Abstract snippets. Kiln geometry not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Wall heat-transfer coefficient for molten plastics: rotary kiln vs falling film
findings.value: about 1000 W/m2K in a rotary kiln vs about 4000 W/m2K in a falling-film reactor
findings.context: Second-hand value cited in a semi-batch plastic heating and melting model
findings.source: Modelling plastic heating and melting in a semi-batch pyrolysis reactor. Applied Energy 2021 (HAL hal-04652254), citing other work
findings.evidence: Search summary: 'about 4000 W/m²K in a falling film reactor versus about 1000 W/m²K in a rotary kiln'

findings.parameter: Li A.M. et al. lab rotary kiln (Zhejiang Univ.), MSW components incl. PE and PVC
findings.value: ID 0.205 m x length 0.450 m (L/D about 2.2); rotation adjustable 0.5–10 rpm, run at 3 rpm; up to 4.5 L of feed per run (batch); externally heated
findings.context: Paper, PE, PVC, rubber, wood, vegetal matter
findings.source: Li A.M. et al. (1999) Experimental studies on municipal solid waste pyrolysis in a laboratory-scale rotary kiln. Energy 24:209–218
findings.evidence: 'internal diameter of 0.205 m and is 0.450 m long ... 0.5 to 10 rpm ... adjusted to 3 rpm ... up to 4.5 litres'

findings.parameter: Li A.M. et al.: effect of final pyrolysis temperature (FPT)
findings.value: Higher FPT raises gas yield and lowers semi-coke yield. Aliphatic content of PE tar first rises, then falls, as FPT rises. A snippet gives gas 9.8% to 88.8% and tar 18.4% to 57.1% over 500–700 °C, but it is unclear whether these are the paper's own data.
findings.context: Same 0.205 x 0.45 m kiln
findings.source: Li A.M. et al. (1999) Pyrolysis of solid waste in a rotary kiln: influence of final pyrolysis temperature on the pyrolysis products. J. Anal. Appl. Pyrolysis 50:149–162
findings.evidence: OSTI abstract; the numeric range is flagged uncertain

findings.parameter: Tyre pilot continuous rotary kiln (Li S.Q. et al.)
findings.value: 450–650 °C; char roughly constant at a mean of 39.8 wt%; maximum oil 45.1 wt% at 500 °C; oil HHV 40–42 MJ/kg, S 0.97–1.54 wt%. A citing study gives kiln D 0.5 m, overall length 3.0 m, feed 10–30 kg/h.
findings.context: Continuous, externally heated pilot (Tsinghua/Zhejiang)
findings.source: Li S.Q., Yao Q., Chi Y., Yan J.H., Cen K.F. (2004) Pilot-scale pyrolysis of scrap tires in a continuous rotary kiln reactor. Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 43:5133–5145
findings.evidence: Abstract gives the yields. Geometry and feed rate are secondary, quoted by a later paper.

findings.parameter: ENEA-Trisaia pilot rotary kiln (tyres)
findings.value: Externally (electrically) heated kiln, D 0.4 m, internal volume 110 dm3 (DERIVED length about 0.88 m), slight over-pressure, 400 L feed hopper; a review gives 3 rpm and 4.8 kg/h; at 500 °C about 45% oil and 44% char (secondary)
findings.context: Continuous pilot, N2 supply; temperature range 698–848 K in the Galvagno 2002 abstract
findings.source: Fortuna F. et al. (1997) J. Anal. Appl. Pyrolysis 40–41:403–417; Galvagno S. et al. (2002) Waste Management 22:917–923
findings.evidence: 'rotary kiln reactor externally heated (110 dm3 in volume and 0.4 m in diameter)'. 3 rpm and 4.8 kg/h come from a 2013 tyre review.

findings.parameter: Mines Albi (RAPSODEE) pilot rotary kiln
findings.value: Ni-Cr tube, ID 0.21 m, length 4 m (4.2 m heated in Colin et al.); 5 independent electric heating zones; max 1000 °C; N2 at +30 mbar; slope 0–7°; rotation 1–21 rpm; loss-in-weight feeder 1–30 kg/h; inner wall may carry a metal grid
findings.context: Continuous pilot used for wood, green waste and pellet pyrolysis/torrefaction and solids-transport studies
findings.source: Descoins N., Dirion J.-L., Howes T. (2005) Chem. Eng. Process. 44:315; Colin B. et al. (Chem. Eng. Trans. 37, 2014); IMT Mines Albi torrefaction page
findings.evidence: 'nickel–chrome hollow cylinder 4 m long with 0.21 m internal diameter ... five independent electric elements ... 30 mbar ... 1000 °C'; Colin: 4.2 m, 0–7°, 1–21 rpm

findings.parameter: Notarnicola et al. ASR bench rotary kiln
findings.value: Kiln 100 cm long x 5 cm diameter; mass flow 200–350 g/h; run time 4–5 h; 450, 550 and 650 °C; gas LHV 18–26 MJ/Nm3 (dry), rising with T
findings.context: Continuous bench kiln, automotive shredder residue (plastic-rich)
findings.source: Notarnicola M. et al. (2017) Pyrolysis of automotive shredder residue in a bench scale rotary kiln. Waste Management 65:92–103 (via review tables)
findings.evidence: Review summary table quoted by search

findings.parameter: Semi-pilot semi-batch rotary kiln (India), mixed plastics and MSW
findings.value: Horizontal stainless-steel tube 1360 mm long, OD 355 mm, wall 3 mm; 450–650 °C; MSW co-pyrolysis at 500 °C and 20 °C/min, 2 kg per run. Mixed plastics give 43 wt% oil and 16 wt% char (another passage: 40–45 wt% oil, 5–7 wt% char). Groundnut shell + HDPE 40:60 at 500 °C gives 49% oil.
findings.context: Semi-batch, rotary, electrically heated (heater type not confirmed)
findings.source: RSC Advances 2026 (paper-mill waste, PMC12927709); Bhatt et al. RSC Adv. 2026, 16:35523 (MSW co-pyrolysis); Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2024 doi 10.1021/acs.iecr.4c03309
findings.evidence: Methods snippet: 'horizontal stainless steel tube measuring 1360 mm in length, with an outer diameter of 355 mm'. Search-engine extraction only, because WebFetch was unavailable.

findings.parameter: Patent US 11319493: continuous catalytic rotary kiln for waste plastic
findings.value: 350–650 °C at 0.0010–0.030 psi gauge. Externally fired annulus burning recycled flue gas. A rotating closed central cylinder 20 cm dia x 230 cm long cut free volume and roughly halved vapour residence time, which reduced excess secondary cracking. Helical wall baffles lengthened solids residence. Condensation at -5 to -15 °C. Problems without these: excess gas, agglomerated lumps, sticky unreacted feed on walls, tar and coke.
findings.context: Plastic + catalyst fed by screw; priority 2018
findings.source: US 11319493 B2, Method for catalytic conversion of waste plastic into liquid fuel
findings.evidence: Quoted patent passages via USPTO PDF extraction. Kiln ID, rpm and yields not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Haloclean (FZK/KIT) reactor concept
findings.value: Gas-tight indirectly heated rotary kiln with a centred co-axial screw that transports hot metal spheres to improve heat transfer to the plastics; two-stage pyrolysis for WEEE (bromine removal); straw run at 450 °C with 40 g/min feed
findings.context: WEEE and biomass; pilot at Forschungszentrum Karlsruhe
findings.source: Hornung A., Seifert H. (2006) Rotary Kiln Pyrolysis of Polymers Containing Heteroatoms, ch. 20 in Scheirs & Kaminsky (eds.) Feedstock Recycling and Pyrolysis of Waste Plastics, Wiley, pp. 549–567
findings.evidence: 'gas-tight rotary kiln fitted with a screw and spheres'. No plastic throughput found.

findings.parameter: Alumina-ball rotary kiln (sticky feed, lignin)
findings.value: Rotating alumina balls prevented char agglomeration and allowed continuous operation without plugging; 550–650 °C with maximum oil at 600 °C; feed 100–200 g/h (sources differ)
findings.context: Bench continuous kiln; analogue for melt and sticky-phase handling
findings.source: Kim et al. (2018) Suppressed char agglomeration by rotary kiln reactor with alumina ball during the pyrolysis of Kraft lignin. J. Ind. Eng. Chem. 66:72–77
findings.evidence: Abstract summary

findings.parameter: DGE Hamm pyrolysis plant: industrial indirectly heated kiln
findings.value: Effective kiln diameter 2.8 m; heated length 20 m (L/D about 7.1); filling degree about 15%; mean residence in heated zone about 90 min; process temperature about 500 °C; kiln shell temperature about 750 °C; 6.65 t/h per kiln; 2 kilns; 100,000 t/a; availability 85%; heating muffle (flue gas); pygas to boiler; operated 2001–2009
findings.context: Continuous, indirectly heated, RDF/MSW at a power plant
findings.source: DGEngineering (2009) Hamm MW pyrolysis plant data sheet (July 2009); DGE reference list
findings.evidence: Data sheet rows: 'Rotary kiln diameter (effective) 2.8 m | Rotary kiln length (heated) 20 m | Filling degree approx. 15 % | Average residence time in heated area approx. 90 min | Process temperature approx. 500 °C | Kiln shell temperature approx. 750 °C' (search-engine extraction)

findings.parameter: Size limits of indirectly heated kilns (designer rule of thumb)
findings.value: Indirectly heated kilns go up to about 3.0 m diameter and 22 m heated length for lifetimes up to 10 years. Directly heated kilns go up to about 6 m diameter and over 50 m long. Pyrolysis kilns typically max about 50,000 t/a per kiln.
findings.context: Industrial practice
findings.source: Gerlach D. (DGEngineering), LinkedIn articles 'Rotary kiln = rotary kiln?' and 'My personal TOP10 rotary kiln pyrolysis plants'
findings.evidence: Search summary of the author's articles

findings.parameter: Burgau MSW pyrolysis plant
findings.value: 2 indirectly heated rotary kilns x 3 t/h (DGE lists 3,500 kg/h); pyrolysis 550 °C; pre-dedusted gas burned at about 1200 °C; 35,000 t/a; feed about 65% domestic, 30% commercial, 5% sewage sludge; operated about 1984/86–2015
findings.context: Continuous, industrial
findings.source: OSTI/ETDE records of the Burgau project reports; DGE reference list
findings.evidence: 'Two indirectly heated rotary kilns in parallel operation, throughput 3 tons/hour each, pyrolysis temperature 550deg C'

findings.parameter: Siemens Schwel-Brenn (Ulm pilot, Fürth 100,000 t/a)
findings.value: Smouldering drum at about 450 °C (some sources 600 °C); 2.5–2.7 t/h or 3 t/h; heating tubes run horizontally inside the drum and carry flue gas; drum slope about 1.5°; about 2 mbar under-pressure at the hot outlet; a drum-seal failure in 1998 caused a gas release and the plant never entered regular operation
findings.context: Continuous, internally tube-heated drum, MSW
findings.source: KIT thesis 'Das Siemens Schwel-Brenn-Verfahren'; patent DE4103605A1; fuerthwiki
findings.evidence: Quoted German passages: 'Die Neigung wird mit 1,5 ° angegeben', 'von etwa 450°C', '2 mbar Unterdruck'

findings.parameter: Mitsui R21 pyrolysis drum (MSW)
findings.value: Drum at 450 °C; waste residence about 1 h; indirectly heated by hot air in many heat-transfer tubes along the drum; Toyohashi 400 t/d (2002); Yame 220 t/d (2000)
findings.context: Continuous industrial, pyrolysis + melting
findings.source: Mitsui, IEA Bioenergy Task 32 presentation 'Pyrolysis Gasification & Melting Process Toyohashi R21 Plant'; UCR/LA County emissions report
findings.evidence: 'gasified at 450ºC in a rotary drum reactor ... heated indirectly by hot air, which passes through a number of heat transfer tubes'; residence about one hour

findings.parameter: Other European waste pyrolysis kilns (throughput)
findings.value: Kiener, Goldshöfe: 2.6 t/h. Salzgitter: 4–6 t/h (timeline lists 7 t/h), 1984/1996. Herne soil cleaning: 5,000 then 9,000 kg/h. Pyropleq-type drums for soil: 3.0–6.5 t/h.
findings.context: Continuous indirectly heated drums
findings.source: DGEngineering 'Pyrolysis rotary kiln developments' timeline and reference pages; Modern Power Systems
findings.evidence: Garbled timeline extraction; values approximate

findings.parameter: Straw pyrolysis 3 MW pilot (Dürnrohr, TU Wien/EVN)
findings.value: Externally heated (jacketed) kiln, 3 MW fuel power, 0.6–0.8 t/h straw, 450–630 °C (up to 650 °C), solids residence 30–45 min (another run: 605 °C, 55 min), chemical efficiency up to 67%
findings.context: Continuous pilot, biomass
findings.source: Kern S., Halwachs M. et al. (2012) J. Anal. Appl. Pyrolysis 97:1–10; Halwachs M. (2011) PhD thesis TU Wien
findings.evidence: Abstract and slides. Kiln D, L and rpm not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Cortus WoodRoll 500 kW pilot (KTH model validation)
findings.value: Indirectly heated kiln; feed 70–90 kg/h (model case 30 kg/h at 2 rpm); solids residence about 1 h; 9 runs of at least 6 h each; flue gas about 420 Nm3/h at 560 °C inlet (secondary, attribution uncertain)
findings.context: Continuous pilot, wood; Saeman granular flow model
findings.source: Babler M.U. et al. (2017) Applied Energy 207:123–133; Phounglamcheik A. et al. (2017) Energy Procedia 105:908–913
findings.evidence: Abstracts plus a secondary snippet

findings.parameter: Chinese commercial continuous rotary kilns for plastics (survey)
findings.value: Henan Doing: continuous rotary kiln, 100 t/d waste plastics, oil 45–52%, carbon black about 30%, gas 18–25%. Kingtiger: continuous, nearly horizontal kiln with catalyst, 50 t/d, mixed plastics 45% oil / 40% carbon black / 15% gas. Niutech: continuous, oil 43–48%, carbon black 32–36%, gas 6–8%. Huayin: catalytic batch, 10 t/batch, 45% oil / 30% carbon black / 10% gas.
findings.context: Industrial units on dirty, real waste (high char/carbon black fraction)
findings.source: Ma J., Zhong Q. (2018/2019) Comparison of Chinese Pyrolysis Processes, Columbia University / WTERT
findings.evidence: Quoted sentences from the paper (search extraction). Yields are company-reported.

findings.parameter: Korean kiln-based plastic pyrolysis: capacity and problems
findings.value: Kiln plants are limited to about 20 t/d because of inefficient heat transfer; residue removal forces frequent shutdowns; operation depends on continuous external heat. A peer-reviewed paper cites a 10 t/d kiln facility limited by low heat-transfer efficiency and states that most industrial plastic pyrolysis reactors are rotary kilns.
findings.context: Korea, industrial
findings.source: KIER press release (EurekAlert / trade reprint); Energy 2023 paper S0360544223029584
findings.evidence: 'processing limited to just 20 tonnes per day due to inefficient heat transfer'. Treat as indicative.

findings.parameter: Mingjie continuous plastics reactor (vendor)
findings.value: MJL-20P fully continuous plastics: reactor 1600 x 26000 mm (L/D about 16), 30 t/d; 16/18 mm wall; 40 t/d for tyres in the same size; semi-continuous MJL-15: 2800 x 7100 mm, 15–16 t/d
findings.context: Commercial continuous rotary reactor; rpm not given
findings.source: Mingjie (ecomingjie.com) product catalogue
findings.evidence: Vendor table via search extraction

findings.parameter: Beston continuous/semi-continuous plastic units (vendor)
findings.value: BLJ-16: batch or semi-continuous, plastics 6–8 t/d (tyres 12–14 t/d); screw-feed limits plastic ≤5 cm and moisture <10%; reuses its own non-condensable gas for heating; oil output at 280–350 °C. BLJ-20 reactor ø2800 x 10000 mm. Fully continuous P30-class: 0.8–1.05 t/h plastic pellets with counter-current hot-air heating, 304/310S reactor.
findings.context: Commercial
findings.source: Beston Group product pages and FAQ
findings.evidence: Vendor pages via search

findings.parameter: Commercial batch rotary drums (tyre/plastic): dimensions and rotation
findings.value: DY-1-6 / DY-1-10 / DY-1-12: 2200x6000, 2600x6600 and 2800x6600 mm; rotation 0.4 r/min; 16 mm Q245R plate; 6 / 10 / 12 t per 24 h; weights 27 / 32 / 35 t; total power 19 kW; batch time 16–20 h. Huayin HY-12T: D2800 x L6600, 40.6 m3, 0.4 r/min; fuel coal, charcoal, gas or oil; 'oil output 80–95%' (vendor claim). Mingjie MJ-12: D2800 x L7100.
findings.context: Batch, externally fired from below (furnace under the rotating drum), horizontal
findings.source: Henan Doing (doinggroup.com, china-doing.com) spec sheets; Huayin listing; Mingjie catalogue
findings.evidence: 'Rotate speed of pyrolysis Reactor 0.4turn/minute'; 'Reactor Size: D2600mm*L6600mm'; 'Total power 19KW'. No vendor source supports a 0.8–1 rpm upper bound.

findings.parameter: Commercial batch drum: cycle and temperatures
findings.value: Feeding about 2 h; heating 8–10 h with the reactor rotating; oil vapour from about 250–280 °C until 350–480 °C; cooling 4–5 h; discharge about 2 h; total 16–18 h (Doing FAQ)
findings.context: Batch tyre/plastic drums
findings.source: Sihai Energy Tech product page; Doing FAQ
findings.evidence: Vendor text via search

findings.parameter: Industrial batch rotary kiln, tyres (academic)
findings.value: 4 t per batch; 400–500 °C; maximum yields about 20% gas, 12% light liquid, 25% heavy liquid, 8% wax, 35% carbon black. A review describes such a kiln as about 2.2 m ID x 6.6 m at 0.5–3 rpm (attribution unverified).
findings.context: Batch rotary kiln, Turkey
findings.source: Ayanoğlu A., Yumrutaş R. (2016) Energy Conversion and Management 111:261–270; Lewandowski W.M. et al. (2019) J. Anal. Appl. Pyrolysis 140:25–53 (review)
findings.evidence: Abstract yields; dimensions from a review snippet

findings.parameter: Japanese plastic liquefaction plants
findings.value: Sapporo Plastic Recycling (Toshiba): 14,800 t/y (initially 13.5 kt/y), degradation vessel of rotary kiln type with triple-vessel structure, 96% reclamation, about 62% oil from household plastic (secondary), PET acids neutralised with alkali, corrosion and clogging solved, plant withdrawn 2010. Niigata: 6,000 t/y, 420 °C in a stirred tank (not a kiln). Mogami Kiko: 3 t/d.
findings.context: Continuous industrial, dechlorinated mixed packaging plastics
findings.source: Fukushima M. et al. (2009) J. Mater. Cycles Waste Manag. 11:11–18; Yamawaki (2009) GEC slides; Juji Lin thesis (Columbia/WTERT)
findings.evidence: 'special designed degradation contrivance that is rotary kiln type with triple vessel structure'. Kiln temperature not found.

findings.parameter: Fuenix Ecogy and Nexus Circular: plastic rotary kiln patents
findings.value: Fuenix Ecogy (Weert, NL): rotary kiln for evaporation of size-reduced thermoplastic waste, with an internal feed conveyor tube running the full length of the shell to melt small flat flakes; a planned second Weert plant of 20,000 t/y (Dow agreement); company reported failed in 2025. Nexus Circular: refractory-lined steel kiln barrel, horizontal or about 10° inclined, taking molten, semi-molten or solid feed, claims 200–1000 °C.
findings.context: Commercial plastic-specific kiln designs
findings.source: US 11988382 B2 (Fuenix Ecogy IP BV); US 12649879 / 12545840 (Nexus Circular)
findings.evidence: Patent abstracts/claims via search. No operating rpm or T found.

findings.parameter: Generic kiln design ranges (reviews/patents)
findings.value: Review: drum 0.5–3 m diameter, 3–20 m long, inclined 1–5°, 1–10 rpm. Patent US 5662052: kiln load below 35%, preferably below about 15%, for adequate mixing and heating; 3–5° slope. Pilot softwood-pellet solids residence 19–37 min, falling with higher rpm. Rotation 0.2–5 rpm in general kiln practice.
findings.context: Slow pyrolysis and waste kilns
findings.source: Advances in slow pyrolysis reactors (2026) ScienceDirect S259017452600721X; US 5662052; Screw reactors and rotary kilns in biochar production, JAAP 2023
findings.evidence: 'kiln load of less than 35% and preferably less than about 15% offers adequate mixing and heating'

findings.parameter: Solid heat-carrier choice
findings.value: Steel balls of 1.0–1.5 mm, or 1 mm quartz or SiC sand; steel balls gave the best results in one study. Steel balls and chains are also used to scrape coke and deposits off walls, because deposits on externally heated kilns drastically inhibit wall heat transfer.
findings.context: Rotary kilns and screws (biochar review); kiln scraping patents
findings.source: Screw reactors and rotary kilns in biochar production (JAAP 2023, LTU OA); US 4147505
findings.evidence: Search summary of the OA review and patents

findings.parameter: Fouling and operational problems reported
findings.value: Wall fouling in an indirectly heated tyre kiln is included in the scale-up model (Proch 2021). Plastic kilns: lumps, sticky unreacted feed on walls, tar and coke (US 11319493). Residues force frequent shutdowns (KIER). Condensers and pipelines clog at low temperature, i.e. wax (KIER CFB paper). Corrosion and clogging, plus organic acids from PET (Sapporo). Seal failure with gas release (Fürth 1998). Air ingress lowers syngas LHV (Perugia kiln thesis).
findings.context: Synthesis of problem reports
findings.source: Proch et al. (2021) Chem. Eng. Sci. 238:116573; US 11319493; KIER; Fukushima 2009; Zajec L. (2009) MSc thesis, Univ. Akureyri
findings.evidence: Abstract and secondary statements

findings.parameter: Mixed plastics oil yield, rotary kilns at about 500 °C (spread)
findings.value: Indian semi-pilot (MSW plastics): 40–45 wt% oil (also 43%). Chinese commercial plants: 43–52% oil. Dalian lab with heat carrier: up to 57.6 wt% at 625 °C. HDPE batch kiln: implied oil+wax about 67% at 480 °C (100 − 32.55% gas, if char is negligible; DERIVED).
findings.context: Spread across kiln types and feed purity
findings.source: Sources as listed in the individual findings
findings.evidence: Compilation

findings.parameter: Tyre rotary kiln: optimum oil temperature (independent kilns)
findings.value: Maximum oil 44 wt% at 550 °C (400–1050 °C scanned); 45.1 wt% at 500 °C (Li 2004); 45.6% at about 500 °C (industrial plant, Northern Cyprus)
findings.context: Tyre kilns, used as an analogue for the oil-maximum location
findings.source: Yazdani E. et al. (2019) Waste Management 85:195–201; Li 2004; LSBU Sustainability 15:14178
findings.evidence: Highlights: 'Maximum oil was achieved at 550 °C'

equations.name: Sullivan–Maier–Ralston mean residence time (USBM 1927)
equations.expression: tau = 1.77 * (L/D) * sqrt(theta) * F / (S * N)
equations.variables: tau mean solids residence time [min]; L heated length and D inner diameter in the same units; theta dynamic angle of repose [deg]; S kiln slope [deg]; N rotation speed [rpm]; F = 1 for an unobstructed kiln (a factor of about 2 for a constricted outlet is quoted in some sources but was NOT verified)
equations.validity: Free-flowing granular solids, no lifters, rolling regime, low slope. The core 1.77*L*sqrt(theta)/(S*D*N) is confirmed by several sources. Melting, sticky plastics break the assumptions, so apply it to the heat-carrier bed only.
equations.source: Sullivan J.D., Maier C.G., Ralston O.C. (1927) Passage of solid particles through rotary cylindrical kilns, US Bureau of Mines Tech. Paper 384; as cited in Liu & Specht (2006) Chem. Eng. Sci. 61:5176

equations.name: Saeman (1951) / Kramers–Croockewit (1952) axial bed-depth profile
equations.expression: dh/dz = -tan(beta)/cos(theta) + [3*tan(theta)*q_v / (4*pi*n*R^3)] * [ (2h/R) - (h/R)^2 ]^(-3/2) ; boundary h(z=0) = h_outlet (dam height or critical depth); hold-up H = integral over L of rho_b*A(h) dz; tau = H/m_dot
equations.variables: h local bed depth [m]; z axial coordinate measured from the discharge end [m]; beta kiln inclination [rad]; theta dynamic angle of repose [rad]; q_v volumetric solids flow [m3/s]; n rotation speed [rev/s]; R inner radius [m]; A(h) bed cross-section area; rho_b bulk density
equations.validity: Rolling or cascading free-flowing beds without lifters. Kramers–Croockewit reproduces bed profiles best (Lebas et al. 1995). The exact form was not verifiable in this session: the search confirmed the tan term and the 3*q/(4*pi*n*R^3) term, and the sign convention depends on the z direction. Check against Liu & Specht 2006 or Descoins 2005 before coding.
equations.source: Saeman W.C. (1951) Chem. Eng. Prog. 47:508; Kramers H., Croockewit P. (1952) Chem. Eng. Sci. 1:259; Lebas E. et al. (1995) Can. J. Chem. Eng. 73:173

equations.name: Rotational Froude number and transverse-motion regime
equations.expression: Fr = omega^2 * R / g ; omega = 2*pi*N/60
equations.variables: omega angular speed [rad/s]; R inner radius [m]; g = 9.81 m/s2; N [rpm]
equations.validity: Mellmann (2001) maps slipping, slumping, rolling, cascading, cataracting and centrifuging from Fr, filling degree and wall friction. A secondary summary gives Fr of about 1e-3 for slipping to cascading. A DEM study cites Fr of about 0.5 for cataracting and 1.5 for centrifuging. The precise rolling-window limits were not retrieved.
equations.source: Mellmann J. (2001) The transverse motion of solids in rotating cylinders—forms of motion and transition behavior. Powder Technol. 118:251–270

equations.name: Circular-segment bed geometry (filling degree, covered wall)
equations.expression: f = (eps - sin eps)/(2*pi) ; h = R*(1 - cos(eps/2)) ; covered-wall fraction = eps/(2*pi) ; bed chord length = 2*R*sin(eps/2)
equations.variables: f filling degree (fraction of cross-section); eps central angle subtended by the bed [rad]; h bed depth at mid-chord; R inner radius
equations.validity: Exact geometry for a flat bed surface (rolling mode). Example: f = 0.12 gives eps of about 1.74 rad and covered wall of about 27.7% of the perimeter.
equations.source: Standard geometry used in rotary-kiln heat-transfer models (e.g. Babler et al. 2017; Liu & Specht 2006)

equations.name: Overall wall-to-waste heat-transfer coefficient (definition used in waste-kiln experiments)
equations.expression: Q_dot = k_mw * A_cw * (T_wall - T_bed) ; measured k_mw = 38.6–50.1 W/m2K (Suzuki 2008) and 153–187 W/m2K (indirectly heated medical-waste kiln, 2025)
equations.variables: Q_dot heat flow to the bed [W]; k_mw overall coefficient [W/m2K]; A_cw covered (wetted) wall area or total inner area, as defined by each source; T_wall inner wall temperature; T_bed bed temperature
equations.validity: Lumped. Values depend on fill, rpm and lifters. Use it as a validation target for the resolved contact, radiation and convection sub-models.
equations.source: Suzuki T. et al. (2008) J. Therm. Sci. Technol. 3:532; Waste Manag. 2025 doi 10.1016/j.wasman.2025.115093

equations.name: Freeboard vapour residence time (plug-flow estimate)
equations.expression: tau_v = V_fb / Q_g ; V_fb = (1 - f) * pi * D^2 * L / 4 ; Q_g = (n_dot_vap + n_dot_N2) * R_u * T / P
equations.variables: tau_v vapour residence time [s]; V_fb freeboard volume [m3]; f filling degree; n_dot molar flows [mol/s]; R_u = 8.314 J/mol/K; T gas temperature [K]; P pressure [Pa]
equations.validity: Order-of-magnitude estimate only; ignores the axial build-up of vapour. Kilns have long vapour residence (minutes at pilot scale), which drives freeboard secondary cracking. Patent US 11319493 halved tau_v with a rotating central insert.
equations.source: Mass balance (derived); concept supported by US 11319493 B2

equations.name: Lifter design guideline (externally heated waste kiln)
equations.expression: About +10% in k_mw if H_l/H_w > 0.45, or if the arc-length ratio lifters/waste-wall interface > 1
equations.variables: H_l lifter height; H_w waste-layer thickness
equations.validity: Single study, waste pyrolysis in an externally heated kiln
equations.source: Suzuki T. et al. (2008) J. Therm. Sci. Technol. 3(3):532–539

key_sources.citation: Kodera Y., Yamamoto T., Ishikawa E. (2021) Energy- and economic-balance estimation of pyrolysis plant for fuel-gas production from plastic waste based on bench-scale plant operations. Fuel Communications 7:100016 (open access)
key_sources.why: Only open-access, plastic-specific, continuous, externally heated kiln with bench geometry (216 x 1000 mm, sand bed retained by end flanges), 1–3.1 kg/h, yields vs T (650–750 °C), and a 200 kg/h industrial design (OD 2.04 m x 4.88 m) with heat losses.

key_sources.citation: DGEngineering (2009) Hamm MW pyrolysis plant data sheet
key_sources.why: Full industrial operating point for an indirectly heated pyrolysis kiln: D 2.8 m, heated L 20 m, fill 15%, 90 min, 500 °C process, 750 °C shell, 6.65 t/h.

key_sources.citation: Zhang Y., Ji G., ..., Li A. (2020) Liquid oils produced from pyrolysis of plastic wastes with heat carrier in rotary kiln. Fuel Process. Technol. 206:106455; and the PSEP 142:203 exergy paper
key_sources.why: Plastic-specific kiln with solid heat carrier: optimum 15% loading, oil maximum 57.6 wt% at 625 °C, rpm and fill tested, energy/exergy self-heating.

key_sources.citation: Suzuki T. et al. (2008) Improvements in pyrolysis of wastes in an externally heated rotary kiln. J. Thermal Sci. Technol. 3:532
key_sources.why: Measured wall-to-waste heat-transfer coefficients vs rpm and lifters, including the plastic-pyrolysis stage; validation target.

key_sources.citation: Li A.M. et al. (1999) Energy 24:209 and J. Anal. Appl. Pyrolysis 50:149, lab rotary kiln (0.205 x 0.45 m, 3 rpm)
key_sources.why: Classic externally heated lab kiln with plastics; geometry and rpm known; FPT trends.

key_sources.citation: Li S.Q. et al. (2004) Pilot-scale pyrolysis of scrap tires in a continuous rotary kiln reactor. Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 43:5133
key_sources.why: Continuous pilot kiln (D 0.5 m, L 3 m, 10–30 kg/h) with yields vs T. Its geometry sets the scale of the recommended pilot reference case.

key_sources.citation: Descoins N., Dirion J.-L., Howes T. (2005) Solid transport in a pyrolysis pilot-scale rotary kiln. Chem. Eng. Process. 44:315; Colin et al. (2014) CET 37
key_sources.why: Well-documented continuous pilot kiln (0.21 m x 4–4.2 m, 5 electric zones, 1–21 rpm, 0–7°, 1–30 kg/h) with RTD/solids-transport data, useful for transport-model validation.

key_sources.citation: Ma J., Zhong Q. (2018) Comparison of Chinese pyrolysis processes (Columbia/WTERT)
key_sources.why: Independent survey of commercial continuous rotary kilns for plastics (Doing 100 t/d, Kingtiger 50 t/d) and batch drums, with product splits.

key_sources.citation: Waste Management 2025: Heat transfer and parameter optimization for medical waste pyrolysis in an indirectly heated rotary kiln
key_sources.why: Quantified dependence of the heat-transfer coefficient on filling (11.3–37.5%), rpm (0.5–3) and heat-source T (700–850 °C) for plastic-rich waste.

key_sources.citation: US 11319493 B2, Method for catalytic conversion of waste plastic into liquid fuel
key_sources.why: Documents plastic-specific kiln problems (lumps, wall sticking, coke) and the effect of reducing freeboard vapour residence time with a rotating insert.

key_sources.citation: Henan Doing / Huayin batch reactor datasheets (DY-1-6/10/12, HY-12T)
key_sources.why: Commercial batch drum geometry (2.2–2.8 m x 6–6.6 m), 0.4 rpm, 16 mm plate, cycle times. Basis for the batch-vs-continuous comparison.

IMPORTANT ACCESS CAVEAT: WebFetch failed with DNS errors (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) for every domain tested: sciencedirect.com, mdpi.com, hal-mines-albi, wikipedia.org and pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov. A proxy diagnostic command was denied by the permission system. So no page in this run was read directly. Every number above came from WebSearch (mostly 'extended' mode), whose engine pulls text from abstracts, open-access full texts, patents and vendor pages. Where the extraction clearly came from a full text (DGE data sheet, patents, PMC methods, the WTERT paper), access is marked 'full-text'. Abstract-page material is marked 'abstract-only', and second-hand citations, news and vendor material 'secondary'. Re-verify the numbers listed in critical_numbers against the PDFs before final use. Most important to check: Kodera 2021 (OA) for rpm, N2 flow and flange; Hamm 2009 PDF; Zhang 2020 for kiln size and heat-carrier type.

CONTINUOUS vs BATCH SUMMARY.
(1) Lab/bench continuous kilns:
- Kodera AIST: 0.216 m OD x 1.0 m, sand bed, 1–3 kg/h, 650–750 °C, PP; gas-dominant yields.
- Notarnicola ASR: 0.05 x 1.0 m, 0.2–0.35 kg/h, 450–650 °C.
- Mines Albi: 0.21 x 4.2 m, 1–30 kg/h, 1–21 rpm, 0–7°.
- ENEA: 0.4 m, 110 L, 3 rpm, 4.8 kg/h.
- Li S.Q. tyres: 0.5 x 3 m, 10–30 kg/h.
(2) Lab batch or semi-batch rotating kilns:
- Li A.M.: 0.205 x 0.45 m, 3 rpm.
- Dalian heat-carrier kiln: 1–6 rpm, 10–20% fill, oil maximum 57.6 wt% at 625 °C.
- Indian semi-pilot: 0.355 m OD x 1.36 m.
- HDPE CFD-DEM study: 480–600 °C.
(3) Pilot or demo continuous units:
- Dürnrohr 3 MW: 0.6–0.8 t/h straw, 30–45 min.
- Cortus 500 kW: 70–90 kg/h, about 1 h.
(4) Industrial continuous units:
- Hamm: 2.8 x 20 m, 6.65 t/h, 500 °C, 750 °C shell, 90 min, 15% fill.
- Burgau: 2 x 3 t/h, 550 °C.
- Schwel-Brenn: about 450 °C, slope 1.5°, 2.5–3 t/h, internal heating tubes.
- Mitsui R21: 450 °C, about 1 h, 220–400 t/d.
- Kiener: 2.6 t/h.
- Sapporo (plastics, rotary-kiln-type triple vessel): 14.8 kt/y.
- Chinese continuous plastic kilns: Doing 100 t/d, Kingtiger 50 t/d, Mingjie 1.6 x 26 m at 30 t/d.
- Korean kiln plants: at most about 20 t/d (heat-transfer limited).
(5) Industrial batch drums: 2.2–2.8 m x 6–7.1 m, 0.4 rpm, 16 mm Q245R, fired from below with coal, wood, gas or oil, 6–12 t per batch, 16–20 h cycles, oil vapour from about 250–280 °C until 350–480 °C. No vendor source found for 0.8–1 rpm. An academic review gives 0.5–3 rpm for a 2.2 x 6.6 m, about 4 t tyre kiln.

CONFLICTS AND SPREAD:
- Rotation speed: 0.4 rpm (big batch drums); 2–4 rpm (lab and pilot; optima reported at 3–4 rpm); up to 21 rpm (Albi capability).
- Fill: 8–15% optimum with heat carriers; 15% at Hamm. The heat-transfer coefficient falls above about 22% fill.
- Process temperatures: 450 °C (MSW drums), 500 °C (Hamm), about 625 °C for the oil maximum with a heat carrier, 650–750 °C for gas.
- Shell to bed ΔT: about 250 K at Hamm.
- Burgau temperature: 550 °C in one report vs 470 °C in the brief (not confirmed).
- Schwel-Brenn: 450 °C vs 600 °C.
- Dalian energy vs exergy efficiency labels are swapped between summaries.
- The Li S.Q. 2004 abstract numbers are mis-attributed to Murillo by some indexes.

GAPS (not found, not invented): plastic flake feed size and bulk density in kilns; purge N2 flow and measured vapour residence times in plastic kilns; wall temperature profiles; Kodera's rpm and N2 flow; Zhang's kiln dimensions and heat-carrier material; Babler and Halwachs kiln D and L; Proch tyre kiln numbers; kiln energy demand in kWh/kg measured for plastics (only Kodera annual balances and the self-heating statements). The Mellmann rolling-regime Fr limits were not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED REFERENCE CASE (continuous, indirectly heated, mixed polyolefin flakes; pilot scale chosen so a resolved 3D CFD fits on a T4 GPU and is anchored to documented pilots):
- Retort: ID 0.50 m, heated length 4.0 m, L/D = 8. Bracketed by Li S.Q. (0.5 x 3 m), Albi (0.21 x 4.2 m) and the Hamm ratio (L/D about 7). Steel wall 10 mm (Kodera retort 0.01 m).
- Slope 1° (Schwel-Brenn 1.5°; reviews 1–5°).
- Rotation 3 rpm. Matches Li A.M. and ENEA at 3 rpm, Suzuki 2.7–4 rpm, and the 4 r/min oil optimum. Fr = (2π·3/60)²·0.25/9.81 ≈ 2.5e-3, a rolling bed.
- Total filling 12%: retained heat-carrier bed (steel balls 1–1.5 mm or silica sand) of about 10% plus plastic, kept in by end dams/narrowed flanges as in Kodera's 110 mm flanges. Matches 15% at Hamm, the 15% Dalian optimum and the patent's <15%; h is highest near 11% fill. The geometry gives a covered-wall fraction of about 27.7%.
- Heating: electric shell in 4–5 zones (Albi-type) or a flue-gas jacket (Kodera heating-gas chamber, Hamm muffle). Shell temperature 600–650 °C; target bed 480–520 °C. For validation of gas yield vs T, also run 600–650 °C cases.
- Feed: 20 kg/h of mixed PE/PP flakes, about 5–20 mm. The size is an assumption; the only sourced limit is the vendor screw-feed limit of 5 cm and <10% moisture. Feed by screw with a gas-tight seal and an N2-purged hopper.
- Solids residence: Sullivan gives about 28 min for theta = 35°, S = 1°, N = 3 rpm and L/D = 8. The target window is 30–60 min (Dürnrohr 30–45 min, R21 about 1 h, Hamm 90 min).
- Purge: co-current N2 of 1–3 Nm3/h (assumed). The plug-flow estimate gives a freeboard vapour residence of about 2–4 min at 500 °C, a long-residence secondary-cracking zone. Offer a central-insert variant (US 11319493) to halve it.
- Heat duty, DERIVED: about 12–16 kW. This assumes cp about 2.3–2.8 kJ/kg/K, melting about 0.1–0.2 MJ/kg and ΔH_pyr 0.92–1.31 MJ/kg from the existing Stoliarov & Walters data. The average flux is about 2–2.5 kW/m2 over 6.3 m2. With h of about 150 W/m2K on the covered wall, the required shell-to-bed ΔT is about 55 K, so the throughput can be raised to 40–60 kg/h for sensitivity runs.

Expected validation trends:
- Gas rises from about 33 wt% at 480 °C to about 56 wt% at 600 °C (HDPE kiln).
- PP: 58.5 / 64.4 / 66.1 wt% gas at 650 / 700 / 750 °C (Kodera).
- Oil maximum about 57.6 wt% near 625 °C with a heat carrier (Dalian).
- Char under 5% for clean polyolefins. Real waste gives 16–40% (Chinese plants, Indian semi-pilot).
- Heat-transfer coefficient 40–190 W/m2K, rising with rpm and falling with fill.

Industrial scale-up variant for figures and video: D 1.6–2.8 m, heated L 12–20 m, fill 15%, 0.5–6.65 t/h, shell about 750 °C, process about 500 °C, residence 60–90 min (Hamm, Mingjie, Kodera 200 kg/h design). Stay within the indirect-kiln limit of about 3 m x 22 m.

Separate from this, list commercial batch drums (2.6 x 6.6 m, 0.4 rpm, fired from below, 16–20 h cycles) as a contrasting design: transient, with a low area-to-volume ratio.

B_bed.topic: TOPIC B: bed mechanics and solids transport in rotary kilns and drums, including transverse regimes, bed depth, residence time, RTD, active layer, plastic melt and sticking behaviour, and DEM feasibility on a T4. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the shared WebSearch budget (200 per turn, across all agents) ran out after 4 searches by this agent. Every WebFetch and curl attempt (mdpi, zenodo, arxiv, iop, academia, cusat, ubc, wikipedia) failed with DNS ENOTFOUND or proxy 403. Only the search-result snippets were actually read. All other numbers are recalled from training knowledge or derived by calculation (scratchpad/kilnB/calc.py), and each one is flagged.

findings.parameter: Froude number definition used for regime maps
findings.value: Fr = omega^2 R / g = (n/n_c)^2, with n_c = (1/2pi) sqrt(g/R)
findings.context: All rotating cylinders. Mellmann 2001 uses R (radius). Some authors use D/2, which gives the same value.
findings.source: Mellmann J. (2001) The transverse motion of solids in rotating cylinders - forms of motion and transition behavior. Powder Technology 118(3):251-270, doi 10.1016/S0032-5910(00)00402-2
findings.evidence: Citation (volume, pages, DOI) confirmed from a Zenodo reference list in search results. The definition form is standard and recalled; the full text was not reachable.

findings.parameter: Rolling regime Froude range and filling degree (Mellmann table)
findings.units: Fr dimensionless; f = filled cross-section fraction
findings.context: Free-flowing granular solids, wall friction above the critical value. This is the regime used for rotary kilns, coolers and dryers.
findings.source: Mellmann 2001, Powder Technol. 118:251-270 (values via a citing paper's summary in search results)
findings.evidence: Search snippet: 'rolling sub-regime (10^-4 < Fr < 10^-2; f > 0.1)' from a paper citing Mellmann. This matches my recollection of Mellmann Table 1.

findings.parameter: Cascading regime Froude range and filling degree (Mellmann table)
findings.context: Curved bed surface (kidney shape). The upper end grades into cataracting.
findings.source: Mellmann 2001 (via a citing paper's summary)
findings.evidence: Search snippet: 'cascading sub-regime (10^-3 < Fr < 10^-1; f > 0.1)'. The rolling and cascading ranges overlap, so the boundary also depends on fill and material.

findings.parameter: Slumping regime Froude range (Mellmann table)
findings.value: 1e-5 < Fr < 1e-3; low filling (recalled as f < 0.1)
findings.context: Periodic avalanching between an upper and a lower angle of repose. Occurs in slow, low-fill kilns.
findings.source: Mellmann 2001, Table 1 (recalled)
findings.evidence: NOT VERIFIED in this session: recalled from training knowledge. The search summary said it could not find the 1e-5 slumping limit in the snippets it saw.

findings.parameter: Slipping regime (sliding / surging) Froude range (Mellmann table)
findings.value: 0 < Fr < 1e-4, occurring when wall friction coefficient mu_W < critical mu_W,c (sliding for f < 0.1, surging for f > 0.1, recalled)
findings.context: Smooth walls or low-friction solids. For polymer pellets on polished steel this is a real risk at low rpm. Lifters or rough walls suppress it.
findings.source: Mellmann 2001, Table 1 (recalled)
findings.evidence: NOT VERIFIED in this session (memory). The regime list 'slipping, slumping, rolling, cascading, cataracting, centrifuging' plus 'sliding' and 'surging' was confirmed from the abstract via search.

findings.parameter: Cataracting and centrifuging Froude limits
findings.value: cataracting about 0.1 < Fr < 1; centrifuging Fr >= 1 (single-particle limit). A study summarising Mellmann's criteria gives cascading-to-cataracting at about Fr = 0.3-0.36.
findings.context: Not relevant for pyrolysis kilns, which run at Fr ~ 1e-3 to 1e-2, but needed for regime checks in the GUI or validation.
findings.source: Mellmann 2001 (recalled) plus a search-result summary of a study citing the 2001 criteria
findings.evidence: Search snippet: 'cascading-to-cataracting transition ... Froude numbers approximately between 0.3 and 0.36'; also 'critical values around Fr ~ 0.001 for slipping to cascading'. The 0.1-1 band is recalled.

findings.parameter: Henein scaling criterion for bed behaviour
findings.value: Similarity of Fr * (D/d_p)^(1/2) and of percent fill is required to scale bed behaviour across particle size and cylinder diameter
findings.context: Continuous pilot kiln and batch rotary cylinders. Materials: nickel oxide pellets, limestone, sand, gravel. Results are plotted as a Bed Behavior Diagram (bed depth vs rotational speed).
findings.source: Henein H., Brimacombe J.K., Watkinson A.P. (1983) Experimental study of transverse bed motion in rotary kilns. Metall. Trans. B 14:191-205
findings.evidence: Abstract (via search): 'scaling of bed behavior with respect to particle size and cylinder diameter requires similarity of Froude number modified by (D/d_p)^1/2, and pct fill'. No numeric boundary curves were obtained.

findings.parameter: Henein model: physics of regime boundaries
findings.value: Slumping/rolling boundary is set mainly by the shear angle and the limiting wedge angle of the slumping segment. The cascading and cataracting boundaries are set by the dynamic angle of repose. Model boundaries agree with the measured ones.
findings.context: Companion modelling paper. Boundaries are plotted as % fill vs Froude number and depend on material friction properties.
findings.source: Henein H., Brimacombe J.K., Watkinson A.P. (1983) The modeling of transverse solids motion in rotary kilns. Metall. Trans. B 14:207-220
findings.evidence: Abstract (via search): 'primary variables are the shear angle and the limiting wedge angle which defines the solids involved in a slump'; 'location of the other boundaries ... determined by the dynamic angle of repose'. The page numbers and the DOI-to-paper pairing are from memory.

findings.parameter: Henein thesis: slumping-to-rolling interpretation
findings.value: Quantitative characterisation of slumping and rolling required a new interpretation of the slumping-to-rolling change
findings.context: UBC PhD thesis (1981), the source of the bed-depth vs speed diagram
findings.source: Henein H., PhD thesis, University of British Columbia (1981)
findings.evidence: Search snippet of the thesis abstract. The full text is open at UBC but the domain was unreachable this session.

findings.parameter: Ding et al. rolling-mode scaling group
findings.value: In rolling mode, Fr, particle-to-drum diameter ratio, % fill and particle restitution coefficient can be combined into a single dimensionless parameter
findings.context: PEPT experiments on rotating drums
findings.source: Ding Y.L., Forster R., Seville J.P.K., Parker D.J. (2001) Scaling relationships for rotating drums. Chem. Eng. Sci. 56:3737-3750 (authors and pages recalled)
findings.evidence: Search snippet of the abstract. The form of the combined group was not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Slumping-to-rolling transition via bed turnover time
findings.value: Bed turnover time is linear in 1/(rotational speed), as predicted by Davidson et al. (2000), and is used to locate the slumping-to-rolling transition
findings.context: DEM thesis summarising Ding et al. (2002) Powder Technol. 124:18-27
findings.source: DEM thesis, CUSAT Dyuthi repository T0653 (author not retrieved)
findings.evidence: Search snippet: 'slumping-to-rolling transition is quantified using bed turnover time, with a linear relationship to the inverse of rotational speed, as predicted by Davidson et al. [2000]'.

findings.parameter: Froude numbers of a pyrolysis-scale kiln (worked example)
findings.context: So 1-3 rpm sits in the rolling band. About 5 rpm reaches the rolling/cascading overlap.
findings.source: This work (derived, scratchpad/kilnB/calc.py)
findings.evidence: Algebra from Fr = omega^2 R/g

findings.parameter: Fill degree vs filling half-angle and bed depth (segment geometry)
findings.context: Flat bed surface (rolling). Gives the covered-wall angle 2*eps and the exposed bed surface (chord) used in the heat-transfer model (Topic C).
findings.source: Circular-segment geometry (derived)
findings.evidence: Computed in calc.py

findings.parameter: Wall-bed contact time per revolution (input to penetration heat-transfer models)
findings.value: t_c = 2 eps / omega. f = 0.05: 12.1 s at 1 rpm, 4.0 s at 3 rpm, 2.4 s at 5 rpm. f = 0.10: 15.5 s at 1 rpm, 5.2 s at 3 rpm, 3.1 s at 5 rpm.
findings.context: Rolling bed with no wall slip. This is the main mechanism by which rotation matters for heat transfer.
findings.source: This work (derived)
findings.evidence: Geometry plus solid-body rotation of the passive layer

findings.parameter: USBM (Sullivan) mean residence time
findings.value: t = 1.77 L sqrt(theta) / (D S n), with t in min, theta = dynamic angle of repose in deg, S = kiln slope in deg, n in rpm, L/D dimensionless. Example L = 10 m, D = 1 m, theta = 35 deg: S = 2 deg gives 52.4 / 26.2 / 17.5 / 10.5 min at 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 rpm.
findings.context: Bare kiln (no dams or lifters), free discharge, shallow rolling bed. Usually quoted as accurate to about +-20-30%.
findings.source: Sullivan J.D., Maier C.G., Ralston O.C. (1927) Passage of solid particles through rotary cylindrical kilns. US Bureau of Mines Technical Paper 384
findings.url: n/a (not retrieved; formula as given in the task brief and recalled)
findings.evidence: Formula from the task brief and memory. Units recalled (theta and S in degrees). The examples are computed.

findings.parameter: Sullivan formula = shallow-bed limit of Saeman (consistency check)
findings.value: Shallow-bed limit of Saeman gives tau = L sin(theta) / (pi n D tan(beta)), i.e. coefficient (180/pi^2) sin(theta) in Sullivan's units. Comparison 1.77 sqrt(theta) vs (180/pi^2) sin(theta): 25 deg 8.85 vs 7.71; 30 deg 9.69 vs 9.12; 35 deg 10.47 vs 10.46; 40 deg 11.19 vs 11.72; 45 deg 11.87 vs 12.90.
findings.context: Agreement is exact at theta = 35 deg and within about 13% for 25-45 deg. The Saeman model therefore reproduces Sullivan, which makes a good validation test.
findings.source: This work (derived from the Saeman equation in the small-eps limit)
findings.evidence: Computed in calc.py. Small-eps expansion: eps - sin eps cos eps ~ (2/3) eps^3 and sin^3 eps ~ eps^3.

findings.parameter: Saeman / Kramers-Croockewit bed-depth profile: worked example
findings.value: 300 kg/h at bulk density 550 kg/m3, D = 1 m, L = 10 m, slope 2 deg, 3 rpm, theta = 35 deg. Normal depth 0.055 m (fill 2.2%). Free discharge (h0 = 5 mm): tau = 17.6 min. Discharge dam h0 = 0.10 m: tau = 22.1 min, mean fill 2.6%. Dam h0 = 0.15 m: tau = 29.8 min, mean fill 3.4%. Sullivan gives 17.5 min.
findings.context: z measured from the discharge end. Dams raise hold-up and residence time locally. Fill depends on feed rate: 1000 kg/h at 2 deg and 1 rpm gives 38% fill (unrealistic), so operating fill must be checked.
findings.source: This work (derived with the ODE in 'equations')
findings.evidence: solve_ivp integration in calc.py

findings.parameter: Typical operating window of rotary kilns
findings.value: Rotation about 0.5-5 rpm; slope about 1-5% (about 0.5-3 deg); fill about 3-15% (up to about 20%); L/D about 5-40 (externally heated kilns at the low end)
findings.context: General rotary kiln practice. Not specific to plastics.
findings.source: Boateng A.A. (2008; 2nd ed. 2016) Rotary Kilns: Transport Phenomena and Transport Processes, Butterworth-Heinemann; Perry's Chemical Engineers' Handbook (recalled)
findings.evidence: NOT VERIFIED in this session (memory). The task brief also states 5-20% fill.

findings.parameter: Active-layer flux balance in a rolling bed (kinematics)
findings.value: Flux per unit length through the active layer at mid-chord: Q = (omega/2) [R^2 - (R cos eps + delta)^2]. Mean active-layer velocity = Q/delta. Example (D = 1 m, f = 0.10, 3 rpm, wall speed 0.157 m/s): delta/h = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 gives Q = 0.019, 0.017, 0.015 m2/s and mean velocity 1.22, 0.55, 0.33 m/s (surface about twice that for a linear profile).
findings.context: Passive region rotates as a rigid body (no wall slip). Exact conservation; delta must come from experiment or a model (Mellmann et al. 2004; Khakhar et al. 1997; Boateng & Barr 1997).
findings.source: This work (derived); framework as in Mellmann/Specht and Khakhar rolling-bed models
findings.evidence: Computed in calc.py. The title 'Prediction of rolling bed motion in rotating cylinders' was confirmed in search results; authors (Mellmann, Specht, Liu, AIChE J. 2004) are recalled.

findings.parameter: Active-layer thickness ratio delta/h
findings.value: No measured value retrieved. Use delta/h ~ 0.1-0.35 as a sensitivity range (own judgement, unverified).
findings.context: Rolling bed at mid-chord. Boateng & Barr (1997, J. Fluid Mech. 330:233-249) measured active-layer velocity profiles in a pilot drum; Ding et al. (2001) and Mellmann et al. (2004) give predictions.
findings.source: Not found in this session
findings.evidence: GAP: needs retrieval of Boateng & Barr 1997, Ding et al. 2001 or Mellmann et al. 2004 tables.

findings.parameter: Axial dispersion: Peclet numbers in rotary kilns
findings.value: NOT RETRIEVED. Recollection only: pilot-kiln RTD studies (Sai et al. 1990, Metall. Trans. B 21:1005-1011; Bongo Njeng et al. 2015, Powder Technol. 269:554-565; Gao et al. 2013, AIChE J.) report near-plug flow with large Pe (order 10^2). Treat as unverified.
findings.context: Free-flowing solids, with and without dams or lifters
findings.source: Sai et al. 1990; Bongo Njeng et al. 2015; Gao et al. 2013 (citations recalled, not checked)
findings.evidence: Memory only. Do not use as a validation target until checked.

findings.parameter: Dams and lifters: effect on transport
findings.value: A discharge dam (or a sticky ring acting as one) sets the bed depth at the discharge end, which raises hold-up and residence time (see worked example: +26% at 0.10 m, +70% at 0.15 m). Lifters lift material into curtains (cascading/showering), increase gas-solid contact, change RTD and add axial dispersion.
findings.context: Chatterjee et al. (1983, Metall. Trans. B 14, Parts I-III) give an empirical tau correlation including dam height, and treat ring formation (Part III). Constants not retrieved.
findings.source: Derived (Kramers ODE) plus Chatterjee et al. 1983 (recalled) plus Bongo Njeng et al. 2015 (lifter shape, recalled)
findings.evidence: ODE results from calc.py; literature constants missing

findings.parameter: Melting and softening temperatures of feed plastics (onset of sticky behaviour)
findings.value: HDPE melts at about 130-137 C; LDPE about 105-115 C; PP about 160-170 C; PS is amorphous with Tg about 100 C and softens or sticks above about 120-150 C
findings.context: With a kiln wall at 450-600 C, plastic in contact with the wall melts within seconds
findings.source: Standard polymer handbook values (recalled)
findings.evidence: NOT VERIFIED in this session (memory)

findings.parameter: Melt viscosity window crossed along the kiln
findings.value: Fresh melt zero-shear viscosity at 300 C: about 100-7000 Pa s (HDPE about 3800, PP about 805 Pa s). Partly cracked melt at about 406 C: about 0.001-0.01 Pa s (expected 0.0032 Pa s).
findings.context: From our stirred-tank model brief (Raju 1979 / patent-based fits plus a chain-length closure). It shows the bed passing from a granular solid to a very viscous sticky paste to a low-viscosity liquid.
findings.source: pirolise_cfd/docs/parameters.json (this project's earlier literature brief: rheology section)
findings.evidence: parameters.json keys feed_eta0_300C_range_Pa_s [100, 7000] and expected_bulk_viscosity_range_Pa_s [0.001, 0.01]

findings.parameter: Wall drag-out (coating) film thickness of the melt
findings.context: Maximum film a wall moving upward at speed U can carry against gravity (Nusselt film: q = U h - rho g h^3/(3 mu), maximised over h). Fresh melt (>10 Pa s) can be carried round the shell as a cm-scale coating, causing wall build-up, rings and an insulating layer. Cracked melt (<0.1 Pa s) pools at the bottom with only a mm-scale wall film.
findings.source: This work (derived lubrication estimate)
findings.evidence: Computed in calc.py. Related literature: rimming and coating flows (Moffatt 1977; Ruschak & Scriven 1976; Thoroddsen & Mahadevan 1997), recalled and not retrieved.

findings.parameter: Melt as binder: agglomeration, wall sticking and ring formation in rotary kilns
findings.value: Aggregate size is controlled by the melt formed in the charge, which acts as a binder; particles also stick to the walls. Kilns develop rings on the inner wall and can suffer sudden shutdown by choking.
findings.context: Generic rotary kiln (patent on predicting safe operating time)
findings.source: US patent application 20250085054, 'Method and system of predicting safe time of operation for a rotary kiln'
findings.evidence: Search snippet quotes: 'melt formed in the mixture, which acts as a binder for particles to grow by sticking to one another'; 'develops a ring within the inner walls and suffers sudden shut down due to choking'

findings.parameter: Effect of wall build-up on heat transfer, and the rotation-speed remedy
findings.value: Material stuck to the kiln wall adds a barrier through which heat must pass. In some cases operators prevent build-up by increasing rotational speed.
findings.context: Vendor guidance (FEECO), generic rotary kilns
findings.source: FEECO International, 'Identifying & Resolving Common Rotary Kiln Processing Challenges'
findings.evidence: Search snippet: 'creates an additional barrier through which heat must pass'; 'operators may be able to prevent slag formation by increasing the kiln's rotational speed'

findings.parameter: Agglomeration of sand heat carrier during waste pyrolysis
findings.value: After a few hours of operation the quartz-sand bed contains agglomerates ('clinkers') that disrupt operation and force shutdown for removal and sand replacement
findings.context: Fluidised bed (not a rotary kiln), solid-waste pyrolysis. Same mechanism (melt-bridged sand) is expected in sand-carrier kilns.
findings.source: US patent 4,448,589, 'Pyrolytic conversion of carbonaceous solids to fuel gas in quartz sand fluidized beds'
findings.evidence: Search snippet quotes 'after a few hours of operation the sand bed contains agglomerates or clinkers'

findings.parameter: Agglomeration in plastic pyrolysis (fluidised bed), recent thesis
findings.value: Thesis on how agglomerates form, how they affect bed heat transfer, and how they break up
findings.context: Fluidised-bed plastic pyrolysis; mechanism relevant to sand or ball carriers in kilns
findings.source: UCL doctoral thesis (2025), 'Experimental characterization of the agglomeration process in fluidized-bed reactors for plastic pyrolysis'
findings.evidence: Title and scope from search snippet

findings.parameter: Rotary-kiln pyrolysis model using sand and polyethylene as model materials
findings.value: Mathematical model and experiments of waste pyrolysis in rotary kilns, using homogeneous model materials (sand, polyethylene) and mixed wastes
findings.context: German doctoral thesis, Bauhaus-Universitaet Weimar (2006). Likely the closest open source for a kiln model with plastic plus inert solid. Not read; author not retrieved.
findings.source: 'Mathematische Modellierung und experimentelle Untersuchungen zur Pyrolyse von Abfaellen in Drehrohrsystemen', Bauhaus-Universitaet Weimar e-pub, 2006
findings.evidence: Search snippet: 'modeled rotary-kiln pyrolysis using homogeneous materials (sand and polyethylene) as well as for mixed wastes'

findings.parameter: Dynamic angle of repose: plastic pellets, flakes and melt
findings.value: NOT FOUND in this session. Unverified working values: polyolefin pellets about 25-35 deg; shredded flakes and film >40 deg and cohesive; low-viscosity melt pool about 0 deg (horizontal free surface); a granular bed wetted by viscous melt bridges has a raised angle and avalanches (slumping or balling) instead of rolling
findings.context: Needed for Saeman (theta) and for regime checks. Must be measured or retrieved; Liu, Specht & Mellmann (2005, Powder Technol. 154:125-131, lower and upper angles of repose, recalled) is the method reference.
findings.source: Own estimate (unverified) plus recalled method reference
findings.evidence: GAP. The linked Powder Technology paper ('Transverse mixing of polymer powders in a rotary cylinder part I: active layer characterization') appeared in search results and may contain polymer-powder angles, but was not read.

findings.parameter: Inert heat carriers (sand, steel or ceramic balls) in plastic pyrolysis kilns
findings.value: Carriers give the melt a large surface to coat, scour the wall, and keep the bed granular so Saeman/rolling kinematics still apply to the carrier. Example recalled: the KIT/FZK 'Haloclean' rotary (screw) kiln used metal balls as heat carrier. No carrier-to-plastic ratios retrieved.
findings.context: Plastic and e-waste pyrolysis
findings.source: Recalled (Hornung et al., Haloclean); not verified
findings.evidence: NOT VERIFIED in this session. GAP: carrier/plastic mass ratio, ball size, wear.

findings.parameter: DEM time step (Rayleigh criterion) and steps per revolution
findings.value: dt_R = pi r sqrt(rho_p/G)/(0.1631 nu + 0.8766), using dt = 0.2 dt_R. dp 4 mm, rho 950, E 1e7 Pa, nu 0.4: dt_R = 1.09e-4 s, 9.2e5 steps/rev at 3 rpm. E 1e8 Pa: 2.9e6 steps/rev. dp 6 mm, E 5e6 Pa: 4.3e5 steps/rev. Sand dp 1 mm, E 1e7 Pa: 2.2e6 steps/rev.
findings.context: Soft-sphere DEM. Reduced stiffness is acceptable for kinematics but not for contact heat conduction without correction.
findings.source: This work (derived); Rayleigh time-step formula recalled (standard in DEM codes)
findings.evidence: Computed in calc.py

findings.parameter: Particle counts for a kiln DEM
findings.value: Per metre of a D = 1 m kiln at f = 0.10 (packing 0.6): dp 3 mm -> 3.3e6; 4 mm -> 1.4e6; 6 mm -> 4.2e5 particles. A full 10 m kiln needs 4e6 to 3e7 particles; adding sand carrier would need far more.
findings.context: Full-kiln DEM is infeasible on a T4 for residence times of 15-60 min
findings.source: This work (derived)
findings.evidence: Computed in calc.py

findings.parameter: GPU DEM throughput on a T4 (feasibility)
findings.value: Own estimate (unverified): about 1e8 particle-steps/s with custom kernels (CUDA, NVIDIA Warp or Taichi) and about 1e7 with plain PyTorch tensor ops. So 1e5 particles at 9e5 steps/rev takes about 15 min/rev (custom) or 2.5 h/rev (PyTorch). 1e6 particles takes about 2.5 h/rev or more. Memory about 0.5 kB per particle, so 1e6 particles needs about 0.5 GB. T4: 2560 CUDA cores, about 8.1 TFLOPS FP32, 16 GB, 320 GB/s (recalled datasheet).
findings.context: GPU DEM codes reach 1e6-1e7 particles on one GPU (Chrono::GPU, Fang et al. 2021, Processes 9:1813; Blaze-DEM, Govender et al. 2016, SoftwareX 5:62; Xu et al. 2011, Particuology, GPU rotating drum; all recalled), but kiln time scales (minutes per revolution, about 1e6 steps/rev) dominate the cost.
findings.source: This work (estimate) plus recalled GPU-DEM literature
findings.evidence: Bandwidth-based estimate; the code throughputs are not verified

equations.name: Froude number and critical speed
equations.expression: Fr = omega^2 R / g ; n_c = (1/(2 pi)) sqrt(g/R) ; Fr = (n/n_c)^2
equations.variables: omega = angular speed [rad/s]; R = inner radius [m]; g = 9.81 m/s2; n = rotational speed [rev/s]
equations.validity: All drums. Regime bands (Mellmann): rolling 1e-4 to 1e-2 (f > 0.1); cascading 1e-3 to 1e-1 (verified via citing paper); slumping 1e-5 to 1e-3, slipping < 1e-4, cataracting 0.1-1, centrifuging >= 1 (recalled)
equations.source: Mellmann 2001, Powder Technol. 118:251-270

equations.name: Henein scale-up group
equations.expression: Keep Fr * (D/d_p)^(1/2) and % fill the same between scales
equations.variables: D = drum diameter; d_p = particle diameter
equations.validity: Slumping/rolling beds of free-flowing solids (NiO pellets, limestone, sand, gravel)
equations.source: Henein, Brimacombe & Watkinson 1983, Metall. Trans. B 14:191-205

equations.name: Bed segment geometry
equations.expression: f = (eps - sin(eps) cos(eps))/pi ; h = R (1 - cos eps) ; chord L_c = 2 R sin eps ; covered wall arc = 2 eps R ; A_bed = R^2 (eps - sin eps cos eps)
equations.variables: eps = half central angle of the bed [rad]; f = fill fraction; h = bed depth at centre
equations.validity: Flat bed surface (rolling, or time-averaged slumping); exact geometry
equations.source: Geometry (derived)

equations.name: USBM / Sullivan residence time
equations.expression: t = 1.77 L sqrt(theta) / (D S n)
equations.variables: t [min]; L, D in the same length unit; theta = dynamic angle of repose [deg]; S = slope [deg]; n [rpm]
equations.validity: Bare kiln, free discharge, shallow rolling bed. Equals the shallow-bed limit of Saeman to within about 13% for theta 25-45 deg (exact at 35 deg).
equations.source: Sullivan, Maier & Ralston 1927, USBM Tech. Paper 384 (recalled; formula from task brief)

equations.name: Saeman / Kramers-Croockewit bed-depth ODE
equations.expression: dh/dz = tan(theta) * [ 3 Phi_v / (4 pi n R^3) * (2h/R - h^2/R^2)^(-3/2) - tan(beta)/sin(theta) ] ; equivalently Phi_v = (4/3) pi n R^3 (tan(beta)/sin(theta) - (dh/dz) cot(theta)) (2h/R - h^2/R^2)^(3/2) (sign set for z increasing upstream)
equations.variables: h(z) = bed depth [m]; z = distance from the discharge end toward the feed [m]; Phi_v = volumetric solids flow [m3/s], which may vary with z as pyrolysis consumes mass; n [rev/s]; beta = kiln inclination [rad]; theta = dynamic angle of repose; BC h(0) = dam height, or about one particle diameter for free discharge
equations.validity: Rolling bed with constant theta, no slip, small beta, cos(beta) ~ 1. Not valid for a liquid melt pool or a sticky bed. Recalled form; checked here for self-consistency (normal-depth limit and Sullivan limit).
equations.source: Saeman 1951, Chem. Eng. Prog. 47:508; Kramers & Croockewit 1952, Chem. Eng. Sci. 1:259 (recalled)

equations.name: Saeman normal depth and shallow-bed residence time
equations.expression: Phi_v = (4/3) pi n R^3 (tan beta / sin theta) sin^3(eps_n) ; tau = integral_0^L A_bed(z) dz / Phi_v ; shallow-bed limit tau = L sin(theta) / (pi n D tan(beta))
equations.variables: eps_n = filling half-angle at normal depth
equations.validity: Uniform bed far from dams; small eps for the limit form
equations.source: Derived from Saeman/Kramers (this work)

equations.name: Rolling-bed active-layer flux balance
equations.expression: Q = (omega/2) [R^2 - (R cos eps + delta)^2] = u_mean,active * delta ; linear profile gives u_surface = 2 u_mean,active ; wall contact time t_c = 2 eps / omega
equations.variables: delta = active-layer thickness at mid-chord [m]; Q = transverse flux per unit kiln length [m2/s]
equations.validity: Rolling mode; passive region in solid-body rotation without wall slip; delta from experiment or model (Mellmann et al. 2004; Khakhar et al. 1997)
equations.source: Kinematic conservation (derived); framework of Mellmann/Specht and Khakhar rolling-bed models

equations.name: Axial dispersion model with Danckwerts boundary conditions
equations.expression: dc/dt + u dc/dz = D_ax d2c/dz2 ; Pe = u L / D_ax ; closed-closed: sigma_theta^2 = 2/Pe - (2/Pe^2)(1 - exp(-Pe))
equations.variables: c = tracer concentration; u = mean axial solids velocity = L/tau; D_ax = axial dispersion coefficient [m2/s]
equations.validity: Fit Pe to RTD data. Rotary kilns are generally near plug flow (high Pe; values not verified this session).
equations.source: Danckwerts 1953, Chem. Eng. Sci. 2:1-13; Levenspiel (standard)

equations.name: Viscous melt drag-out film on the rising wall
equations.expression: q = U h - rho g h^3/(3 mu) ; maximum at h* = sqrt(mu U/(rho g)), q_max = (2/3) U h*
equations.variables: U = omega R = wall speed; mu = melt viscosity; rho = melt density; h = film thickness
equations.validity: Lubrication (thin film, low Re) estimate of how much melt the shell can carry. Indicates a coating or ring regime for mu >~ 10 Pa s and a pool with a thin film for mu <~ 0.1 Pa s.
equations.source: Derived (classic Nusselt/Moffatt coating-flow reasoning)

equations.name: Rayleigh DEM time step
equations.expression: dt_R = pi r sqrt(rho_p / G) / (0.1631 nu + 0.8766), with G = E/(2(1+nu)) ; use dt ~ 0.1-0.3 dt_R
equations.variables: r = particle radius; rho_p = particle density; E = Young's modulus; nu = Poisson ratio
equations.validity: Hertz-type soft-sphere DEM
equations.source: Standard DEM practice (recalled)

equations.name: Friedman & Marshall residence time for flighted drums (lifters, gas flow)
equations.variables: tau [min]; L, D [ft]; S [ft/ft]; N [rpm]; G = gas mass velocity [lb/(h ft2)]; F = feed rate [lb/(h ft2)]; d_p [micron]; + for counter-current gas, - for co-current
equations.validity: Flighted rotary dryers. Use only if lifters are added. Recalled from Perry's; unverified.
equations.source: Friedman & Marshall 1949, Chem. Eng. Prog. 45 (as given in Perry's Handbook; recalled)
