findings.context: T = m g r_cg sin(beta), P = 2 pi n T/60. Matches vendor 4-5.5 kW motors and 19-30 kW total installed power. Flights add torque from the material they hold on the rising side; seal friction and roller friction add more.
findings.source: Derived (this work); thermal duty from Gamboa et al. 2023
findings.evidence: Python calculation

findings.parameter: DERIVED: consistency check of empirical drive formulas with the CoG-torque physics
findings.value: Allis-Chalmers K = 0.00076 (Load HP = (D sin theta)^3 N L K, ft) is exactly T = rho_b g L c^3 sin(beta)/12 with rho_b = 75 lb/ft3 (1200 kg/m3) and beta = 40 deg. The 0.356 constant in P1 = 0.356 M D N K1 [HP] implies r_cg sin(beta) = 0.258 D.
findings.context: So the industrial rules are the bed-torque equation with a typical density and repose angle built in; for light plastic or tyre beds, rescale by rho_b and sin(beta)
findings.source: Derived (this work) from slideshare 'Formulas kiln' and the Scribd rotary dryer power sheet
findings.evidence: Python calculation

equations.name: Penetration-theory wall-to-bed contact HTC
equations.expression: h_ws = 2*sqrt(lambda_b*rho_b*c_p,b/(pi*t_c)) ; series form with contact resistance: 1/h_ws = 1/h_contact + 1/h_pen (Schlünder-Mollekopf / Li et al.)
equations.variables: lambda_b, rho_b, c_p,b = bed effective conductivity, bulk density and heat capacity; t_c = contact time of covered wall with bed (s)
equations.validity: Rolling/cascading bed with good transverse mixing; overestimates at very short t_c unless the first-particle contact resistance is added; measured values scale roughly with sqrt(n)
equations.source: Moumin et al., IJHMT 177 (2021) 121473; Herz et al. CES 82 (2012) 312-318

equations.name: Contact time per revolution
equations.expression: t_c = gamma*60/(2*pi*n)  (gamma in rad, n in rpm); revolution period T_rev = 60/n
equations.variables: gamma = filling (central) angle of the bed, n = rotational speed
equations.validity: Rolling regime, no slip at the wall
equations.source: Moumin et al. 2021

equations.name: Filling degree vs central angle; bed centroid; bed torque; power
equations.expression: F = (eps - sin eps)/(2*pi) ; r_cg = 4*R*sin^3(eps/2)/(3*(eps - sin eps)) ; T = m_bed*g*r_cg*sin(beta) = (2/3)*rho_b*g*L*R^3*sin^3(eps/2)*sin(beta) = rho_b*g*L*c^3*sin(beta)/12 ; P = 2*pi*n*T/60
equations.variables: eps = full central angle of the bed segment (rad), R = drum radius, L = filled length, c = chord = 2R sin(eps/2), beta = dynamic angle of repose, rho_b = bulk density, n in rpm
equations.validity: Flat-surface rolling bed in an unflighted drum (exact circular-segment geometry). Flights add the torque of the material they hold up. Add support-roller and seal friction and the gear efficiency for motor size.
equations.source: Derived (standard circular-segment geometry); consistent with Allis-Chalmers load-HP form and Liu et al. 2016 mechanistic basis

equations.name: Allis-Chalmers load horsepower
equations.expression: Load HP = (D*sin(theta))^3 * N * L * K, K = 0.00076 ; plus friction HP from roller loads (friction coefficient 0.018 quoted) ; motor rated for 4/3 x normal-speed HP
equations.variables: D = inside (lining) diameter ft, theta from chart vs % kiln load (D sin theta = bed chord), N = rpm, L = length ft
equations.validity: Imperial units; K implies rho_b about 75 lb/ft3 and repose about 40 deg (derived); OCR-garbled source
equations.source: Allis-Chalmers bulletin as reproduced in 'Formulas kiln' and pdfcoffee copy

equations.name: CE Raymond / Perry's rotary drum drive power
equations.variables: N = rpm; d = shell diameter ft; w = material (live) load lb; D = riding-ring diameter ft (the snippet garbled this term; definition from Perry's); W = total rotating load (equipment + material) lb
equations.validity: Flighted rotary dryers/kilns; empirical
equations.source: Kelly/Mujumdar, Handbook of Industrial Drying, ch. 7 Rotary Drying (citing CE Raymond Div., Combustion Engineering)

equations.name: Dryer material-movement power (design sheet)
equations.expression: P1[HP] = 0.356*M*D*N*K1 ; total = P1 + roller friction term + rotation term ~ (M + W), divided by transmission efficiency
equations.variables: M = material hold-up (t), D = shell diameter (m), N = rpm, K1 = material action factor 0.6-1.0
equations.validity: Empirical; 0.356 implies r_cg*sin(beta) = 0.258 D (derived)
equations.source: Rotary dryer design and power calculations (Scribd)

equations.name: Static-layer conduction time and penetration depth
equations.expression: t_pen ~ L^2/alpha_b ; delta(t) = sqrt(pi*alpha_b*t) ; alpha_b = k_eff/(rho_b*c_p)
equations.variables: L = layer thickness from heated wall, k_eff = static bed conductivity (about 0.05-0.2 W/mK for plastic flakes)
equations.validity: Order-of-magnitude; ignores latent heat of melting, the pyrolysis endotherm and melt convection
equations.source: Standard transient conduction (derived)

equations.name: Wall superheat for constant flux into a static semi-infinite bed
equations.expression: T_w(t) - T_0 = 2*q*sqrt(t/pi)/e ; e = sqrt(k*rho*c_p)  (rotating, quasi-steady: T_w - T_bed = q/h_ws)
equations.variables: q = wall heat flux W/m2, e = bed thermal effusivity
equations.validity: Semi-infinite static bed; in reality capped by the flue-gas/burner temperature
equations.source: Standard transient conduction (derived)

equations.name: Lumped heating time of a mixed rotating bed
equations.expression: tau = m_bed*c_p/(h_ws*A_cw) ; A_cw = eps*R*L
equations.variables: A_cw = covered-wall area, h_ws from penetration model
equations.validity: Well-mixed bed (heating time much longer than mixing time); freeboard radiation to the bed surface adds a parallel path
equations.source: Derived

equations.name: Emady heating-time scaling
equations.expression: tau/tau_c = F(phi), phi = tau_p/tau_c
equations.variables: tau = bed heating time, tau_p = particle thermal time constant, tau_c = particle-wall contact time
equations.validity: DEM, conduction-only drums over a wide range of rpm and conductivity
equations.source: Emady et al., CES 152 (2016) 45-54

equations.name: Zehner-Schlünder effective conductivity of a packed bed
equations.expression: k_e/k_g = (1 - sqrt(1-psi)) + (2*sqrt(1-psi)/N)*[ (1-1/kappa)*B/N^2*ln(kappa/B) - (B+1)/2 - (B-1)/N ], N = 1 - B/kappa, B = C*((1-psi)/psi)^(10/9), kappa = k_s/k_g
equations.variables: psi = porosity, C = 1.25 spheres (1.4 broken particles), k_s = solid, k_g = gas conductivity
equations.validity: Static packed bed without radiation or flattening coefficient
equations.source: Zehner & Schlünder (1970); Tsotsas & Martin (1987) review

equations.name: NFPA 69 O2 margin
equations.expression: O2_max = LOC - 2 vol% (LOC >= 5 %, monitored) or 0.6*LOC (LOC < 5 %); unmonitored: LOC - 4.5 vol% (LOC >= 7.5 %) or 0.4*LOC
equations.variables: LOC = limiting oxygen concentration for the worst-case gas (H2: 5 vol%)
equations.validity: Inerting design under NFPA 69

critical_numbers: Static plastic-flake bed k_eff about 0.05-0.14 W/mK (Zehner-Schlünder, derived); bed alpha about 1.75-2.5e-7 m2/s
Static heating time t ~ L^2/alpha: 0.1 m about 11-16 h; 0.3 m about 100-143 h (derived)
Rotating at 0.4-1 rpm: contact time 16-59 s, h_pen about 47-93 W/m2K, lumped bed heating 0.5-2 h in a 2.6 x 6.6 m drum (derived)
Transverse mixing complete within about 2 revolutions with strips at >5 rpm and <15 % fill (Wes et al. 1976)
Nafsun 2017 test range: n = 1-6 rpm, F = 10-20 %, drum 0.6 m x 0.45 m
Batch tyre drum: 2.6 m x 6.6 m, 0.4 rpm, 10 t/24 h, 19 kW total installed, batch 16-20 h (Doing)
Bangladesh commercial batch rotary drum: 4.5 t/run, 420 C, +0.03 bar, burners on oil for 3 h then gas for 5 h; oil 45 wt%
Typical tyre yields (rotary, about 450 C): oil 40 +/- 4, rCB 45 +/- 4, gas 15 +/- 3 wt%; steel 8-15 wt% of whole tyres
Tyre pyrolysis heat demand 1.41-2.16 kJ/g; 30-50 % of the pyro-gas covers it; 10 t batch about 390-750 kW over 8-10 h
O2 <= 1 % (patent target); pressure about +/-3 in WC (+/-0.75 kPa); alternative -0.02 to -0.1 in WC
NFPA 69: O2 at least 2 vol% below LOC (monitored, LOC >= 5 %), or <= 60 % LOC; LOC(H2) = 5 %, LOC(CH4) = 12 %
Seal relative leakage: labyrinth >> 5 %, single leaf 3-5 %, double leaf about 25 % of single, graphite-face bellows << 1 %
Bed torque T = m g r_cg sin(beta); r_cg = 0.30-0.35 D at 20-30 % fill; 10 t in a 2.6 m drum: T = 38-57 kN m, P = 1.6-2.4 kW at 0.4 rpm
Drive power about 0.2-1.2 % of thermal duty for batch tyre drums (derived); vendor motors 4-5.5 kW
Motor sized for 4/3 x normal-speed power; starting torque up to 250 % (Metso) or 3-5x running
6 m x 60 m kiln: about 800 kW at 3 rpm (about 2.55 MN m)
sweep.notes:
TOOLING CAVEAT: I could not read any full text. WebFetch failed with DNS ENOTFOUND on every domain tried (sciencedirect, researchgate, arxiv, ncbi, up.ac.za), and direct curl was blocked by the egress proxy (403). Every number therefore comes from WebSearch extracts: abstracts, highlights, patent text and vendor pages. Access is marked 'abstract-only' or 'secondary', and nothing was verified against tables in full text. Items labelled 'DERIVED' are my own calculations (Python, inputs stated) and are not literature values.

Priority items to verify in full text: (a) the coefficients of the Liu et al. 2016 power-draw regression and the 70-75 % share; (b) the h_ws values in Herz et al. 2012 (expected tens to a few hundred W/m2K); (c) the char, gas and steel split in Islam et al. 2013; (d) the D-term definition in the CE Raymond/Perry equation (riding-ring diameter, per Perry's); (e) LOC for ethylene and CO.

Gaps:
- No paired static-vs-rotating pyrolysis experiment with yields was found. The closest are Aylón 2008 (fixed vs moving bed, tyres), the stirred vs unstirred microwave LLDPE study, and the Hedlund accident, where the non-rotating heated reactor's wall exceeded the gas autoignition temperature. For the 'static vs dynamic' panel, the quantitative case rests on time scales: static conduction takes tens to hundreds of hours for 0.1-0.3 m layers with k about 0.1 W/mK; a rotating bed is renewed every 60-150 s per revolution and mixes in a few revolutions.
- No measured effective conductivity of a plastic-flake bed was found. The Zehner-Schlünder estimate (0.05-0.14 W/mK without radiation) supports the brief's 0.1-0.2 W/mK once radiation at 400-500 C is added.

Modelling advice for the Colab/Star-CCM+ model:
- Use the penetration-model h_ws (with optional contact resistance) as the wall-to-bed boundary condition, and the CoG torque equation for drive power.
- For plastics, the bed becomes a viscous, sticky melt above about 130-170 C. Flights then cannot cascade it the way the KINTEK infographic shows for granular solids such as tyres, so the cascading/flight model applies mainly before melting and to the char.
- Batch 'fuel oil + carbon black' drums run at about 0.4 rpm with direct burners underneath and a flue-gas jacket. Their slight positive pressure (0.03 bar in the Bangladesh plant) contrasts with the patent advice of near-neutral +/-3 in WC; both aim to keep O2 at or below about 1-2 vol%, consistent with the NFPA 69 margin for H2-containing gas.

verdict_blocked_network.summary:
I could not open any full text. WebFetch failed with DNS ENOTFOUND on every domain, curl through the proxy returned 403 for all journal, patent and wiki hosts, and the shared WebSearch budget ran out after about 18 searches. Every verdict below rests on search extracts I saw myself, or on my own recomputation. Items I could not see are marked unverifiable.

Confirmed from abstract or patent extracts:
- Nafsun 2017: 1-6 rpm, 10-20 % fill, 0.6 x 0.45 m drum, all trends.
- Wes 1976: transverse mixing done in 2 revolutions, valid only above 5 rpm and below 15 % fill.
- Herz 2012 IJHMT test matrix: 1/3/6 rpm, 10/15/20 % fill, 0.7/1.3/2.0 mm particles, three materials, one of four models agreed. The 600 x 450 mm dimensions were not seen for this paper.
- Emady 2016 time-scale collapse.
- Yánez 2013 melt diffusivities, 6.92e-7 and 5.53e-7 m2/s. These look about 5x high against typical PE melt properties.
- Islam 2013 Bangladesh plant: 4.5 t/run, 420 C, 0.03 bar, 3 h on oil then 5 h on gas. The 45/35/10/10 split is in the abstract itself. The 6 m x 2 m dimensions were not seen.
- Gamboa 2023: 1.41-2.16 kJ/g, 30-50 % of the gas, 37.3 MJ/kg.
- US 8,888,961: O2 at or below 1 %. US 9,777,159: +/-3 in WC in a claim. US 5,167,772: -0.02 to -0.1 in WC with plug seals.
- NFPA 69 margins, from secondary extracts only.

Corrected:
1. Hedlund. The thread merged two incidents. The 2-minute purge and the unverified 40 kPa step belong to 2021, with about 7 t of baled plastic loaded. The underside-heating and autoignition explanation belongs to 2020.
2. Static penetration times. The stated inputs give alpha of 1.25-3.5e-7, not 1.75-2.5e-7, so 0.1 m takes 7.9-22 h and 0.3 m takes 71-200 h. The molten-layer times are probably 4-6x too short.
3. Drive torque. 10 t at 20-30 % fill needs a bulk density of 950-1430 kg/m3. At a realistic 350-550 kg/m3, 10 t fills 52-82 % of the drum, torque is 10-34 kN m and power 0.4-1.4 kW at 0.4 rpm. The duty ratio upper bound is 1.5 %, not 1.2 %. The conclusion that drive power is tiny next to thermal duty still holds.

Unverifiable: about 30 items. These include the 4 %/18 % baffle figures (not found even by exact-phrase search; drop them), the Moumin penetration formula as attributed (the formula is standard and dimensionally correct), the chi range, the Liu 2016 70-75 % share, all vendor specs and seal-leakage figures, the LOC table and the Wikipedia 800 kW value.

My own checks of the derived calculations (Zehner-Schlünder, rotating-bed renewal, wall superheat, the segment and torque algebra, the Allis-Chalmers K identity) all came out right.

Key addition, Moumin 2021: for a cohesive powder the measured wall-to-bed coefficient fell far below penetration theory, and longitudinal strips raised it 2-3x. For sticky or melting plastic, h_ws should be reduced unless flights are modelled.

The 2017 CES journal text itself is paywalled; CORE and Semantic Scholar list no readable copy.

Two 2017 statements were NOT seen and stay unverified: that fill has no significant effect at high rpm, and that the data agree with the penetration model at low rpm. The 2015 paper also says the number of drum revolutions needed to mix RISES with rpm (Fig. 8). The 59 s example is about 6 revolutions in a smooth drum.

verdicts.claimed: Passive layer: T falls from the wall to the active/passive boundary; active layer: T rises to the surface; smaller gradient in the upper bed

Moumin et al. 2021 (Sec. 3.4, Fig. 3.4) found that in rolling sand at 1 rpm the highest temperatures were at the wall and the lowest in the upper core, 'similar to a fixed bed', with only a thin active layer mixing. Nafsun et al. 2014 found bed temperature decreasing with distance from the wall.

verdicts.parameter: Herz et al. 2012 IJHMT 55: contact heat-transfer test matrix
verdicts.claimed: D 600 mm, L 450 mm; 1/3/6 rpm; F 10-20 %; d_p 0.7-2.0 mm; quartz sand, glass beads, copper beads; one of four models agreed
verdicts.source_checked: Paper is paywalled and Semantic Scholar has no abstract. The group's drum was checked in Nafsun et al. HEFAT 2014 (UPSpace 2263/44635, full text).
verdicts.note: The group's batch drum (steel, 2 mm wall, ID 600 mm, L 450 mm, 3 electric heaters totalling 4.5 kW, up to 200 C) is confirmed. The companion 2014 paper (F 20 %, 1 and 6 rpm, six materials) found good agreement with TWO of four models (Li et al. 2005 and Schlunder-Mollekopf), not one.

verdicts.parameter: Herz et al. 2012 CES 82: extended penetration theory, chi = 0.096-0.198
verdicts.claimed: chi about 0.096 < chi < 0.198
verdicts.source_checked: Paper is paywalled. Context comes from Moumin et al. 2021, Table 1 (full text).
verdicts.note: Moumin Table 1 gives the same series form, alpha_ws = (chi*d_p/lambda_g + 1/alpha_pen)^-1, with chi = 0.085 (Sullivan and Sabersky 1975) and chi = 0.1 (Li et al. 2005). A fitted chi of 0.1-0.2 is therefore plausible, but the 0.096-0.198 range itself was not seen.

verdicts.parameter: Penetration HTC alpha_pen = 2*sqrt(lambda*rho*c_p/(pi*t)), t = gamma*60/(2*pi*n), attributed to Moumin et al. 2021
verdicts.claimed: Equation and contact time as stated
verdicts.source_checked: Moumin, Tescari, Sattler, IJHMT 177 (2021) 121473, full open-access PDF (elib.dlr.de/145982): Eq. (2.3) and Eq. (2.4); Eq. (2.2) F = (gamma/2 - sin(gamma/2)cos(gamma/2))/pi
verdicts.note: gamma is the FULL filling angle in rad and n is in rpm; lambda, rho and c_p are BULK (bed) properties. Nafsun 2014 writes the same thing as t = gamma/(pi*n) with gamma the HALF angle (F = (gamma - sin gamma cos gamma)/pi) and n in 1/s, so do not mix the two conventions. Independent check: this formula reproduces the 'Wes et al.' column of Nafsun 2014 Table 2 within 1-3 % for 5 of 6 materials (see additional findings).

verdicts.parameter: 'Measured coefficients plot as straight lines against sqrt(n)' (attributed to Moumin 2021)

verdicts.corrected_value: The arithmetic is right (recomputed 47-93 W/m2K). verdicts.parameter: Equation: CE Raymond / Perry drive power
verdicts.claimed: bhp = N(4.75 d w + 0.1925 D W + 0.33 W)/100000, D = riding-ring diameter

additional_findings.parameter: Measured wall-to-bed (contact) HTC, indirectly heated batch drum, F = 20 %
additional_findings.value: Measured (n 1 rpm / 6 rpm): steel spheres 173-259 / 213-320; animal powder 65-98 / 127-190; cement clinker 54-82 / 80-120; expanded clay 27-41 / 36-54; quartz sand 81-122 / 198-298; glass beads 60-90 / 85-127. Model columns (Wes/penetration; Tscheng-Watkinson; Schlunder-Mollekopf; Li) at 1 rpm for expanded clay: 49, 33, 40, 31; at 6 rpm: 120, 56, 76, 50.
additional_findings.context: Drum ID 0.6 m, L 0.45 m, 2 mm steel wall, 4.5 kW electric heating, up to 200 C. Bed properties (Table 1): d_p, bulk density, c_p, lambda = steel 2.0 mm, 4827, 465, 1.37; animal powder 0.4 mm, 574, 1538, 0.12; clinker 4.5 mm, 1478, 917, 0.20; expanded clay 3.0 mm, 432, 769, 0.12; glass beads 2.0 mm, 1680, 800, 0.25; quartz sand 0.2 mm, 1590, 1080, 0.30 (units mm, kg/m3, J/kg K, W/m K). Regression scatter about +/-20 %. Expanded clay (light, low-k, mm-size) is the closest open analogue for plastic pellets or flakes before melting.
additional_findings.source: Nafsun A.I., Herz F., Specht E., Scherer V., Wirtz S., The contact heat transfer in rotary kilns and the effect of material properties, HEFAT 2014, Orlando
additional_findings.evidence: Table 1 (materials) and Table 2 (experimental vs model h_ws); Eqs (2)-(4) series contact + penetration model; Fig. 8

additional_findings.parameter: DERIVED: check of the penetration formula and contact time against Nafsun 2014 Table 2
additional_findings.value: h_pen = 2 sqrt(lambda rho c_p/(pi t)), t = eps*60/(2 pi n), with eps = 121.1 deg for F = 20 %. Results: steel 440/1079, animal 82/200, clinker 131/320, expanded clay 50/123, glass 146/357 at 1/6 rpm, vs tabulated 'Wes et al.' 440/1079, 83/204, 132/323, 49/120, 146/359. Quartz sand reproduces the table (106/260) only with lambda 0.10 and rho 1640 (the 2015 paper's values), not with Table 1's 0.30/1590.
additional_findings.context: Confirms the equation, the full-angle/rpm form of the contact time, and that Wes et al. means pure penetration theory. Ready-made validation case for the Colab wall-to-bed BC.
additional_findings.source: Derived (this verification) from Nafsun et al. HEFAT 2014 Tables 1-2
additional_findings.evidence: Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/hv_calc/pen.py

additional_findings.parameter: DERIVED: realistic wall-to-bed HTC for a light, mm-size (plastic-like) bed in a 2.6 m batch drum
additional_findings.value: Series contact coefficient backed out from the expanded-clay data: about 50-250 W/m2K (central 70-110). Predicted h_ws at F 20 %, 0.4 rpm is about 22-24 W/m2K. Range 20-40 W/m2K for 0.4-1 rpm, against pure penetration 47-93 W/m2K.
additional_findings.context: Uses 1/h = 1/h_c + 1/h_pen with h_pen proportional to sqrt(n). Contact time does not depend on drum diameter, so the 0.6 m data transfer to 2.6 m at equal F and n. Valid only before melting. Sticky melt makes it worse (see the Moumin cohesive powder case).
additional_findings.source: Derived (this verification) from Nafsun et al. 2014 Table 2
additional_findings.evidence: Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/hv_calc/budget.py

additional_findings.parameter: Moumin et al. 2021: measured h_ws for rolling sand, cohesive powder and the effect of strips
additional_findings.value: Sand (200 um, 1397 kg/m3, 0.27 W/m K), F 10 %, 1 rpm: mean 136.5 W/m2K, raw range 64-184, plate means 132/139/134 (penetration theory about 154, my calculation). Cement raw meal (15 um, 932 kg/m3, 0.14 W/m K) without built-ins: sliding motion; h_ws at 40 C about 2.5x below models at 1 rpm, up to 4x at higher rpm, up to 6x overall; rpm had no significant effect. Six or twelve 2 mm longitudinal strips raised h_ws by 2.2/2.9/3.1x at 1/2/3 rpm (F 5 %) and about 2x at F 10 %, with no difference between 6 and 12 strips. With strips, h rises with rpm.
additional_findings.context: Cylinder 250 mm ID x 500 mm, 2 mm stainless wall, heating cable up to 6.5 kW, target 120 C; 1/2/3 rpm; F 5 and 10 %. Measured h_ws fell with rising bed temperature (attributed to thermocouple lag and convective losses). Key for plastics: a non-rolling (slumping or sliding) bed gets 2.5-6x less wall heat than penetration theory; even small strips restore it.
additional_findings.source: Moumin G., Tescari S., Sattler C., Impact of bed motion on the wall-to-bed heat transfer for powders in a rotary kiln and effect of built-ins, IJHMT 177 (2021) 121473
additional_findings.evidence: Sec. 3.5 (136.5 W/m2K), Table 3.1, Sec. 4.2 and Figs 4.3-4.5 (factors 2.2, 2.9, 3.1; about 2), Conclusions

additional_findings.parameter: Wall-to-bed correlation constants (Moumin 2021, Table 1 and Appendix A.1)
additional_findings.value: Tscheng-Watkinson: alpha_ws = 11.6 (lambda_s/l_gamma)(omega R^2 gamma/a_s)^0.3, with l_gamma the covered-wall arc. Sullivan-Sabersky: alpha_ws = (chi d_p/lambda_g + 1/alpha_pen)^-1, chi = 0.085. Li et al. 2005: same form, chi = 0.1. Lehmberg: h* = 3607 1/m for sand d_p 157 um. Wachters-Kramers: valid below 9.5 rpm. Schlunder-Mollekopf: alpha_ws = (1/alpha_con + 1/alpha_pen)^-1 with alpha_con = phi alpha_wp + (1-phi) 2(lambda_g/d_p)/(sqrt2 + (2l+2delta)/d_p) + alpha_rad and coverage phi about 0.8; alpha_wp = 4(lambda_g/d_p)[(1 + 2(l+delta)/d_p) ln(1 + d_p/(2(l+delta))) - 1]; l = 2(2-gamma*)/gamma* sqrt(2 pi R T/M) lambda_g/(p(2c_p,g - R/M)); log(1/gamma* - 1) = 0.6 - (1000 K/T + 1)/2.8; alpha_rad = 4 C12 T^3 with C12 = sigma/(1/eps_w + 1/eps_s - 1).
additional_findings.units: W m^-2 K^-1 (constants dimensionless or as given)
additional_findings.context: Wes et al. (penetration only) and Tscheng-Watkinson bracket the predictions; Schlunder-Mollekopf gives the highest of the contact-resistance models. Wachters-Kramers strongly underpredicts and was dropped.
additional_findings.source: Moumin et al. 2021, IJHMT 177, 121473
additional_findings.evidence: Eq. (2.1), Table 1, Appendix A.1 Eqs (A.1)-(A.5)

additional_findings.parameter: Model overestimation for slumping or sliding beds (Herz et al. 2015)
additional_findings.value: Slumping and sliding motions: literature models overestimate h_ws by about 3x and 5x; rolling agrees
additional_findings.context: Reported in Moumin 2021's review of Herz et al., Exp. Heat Transfer 28 (2015) 174-188 (not opened). Wes et al. (1976, Powder Technol. 13:185) with 9 shovel-type built-ins measured h_ws in agreement with penetration theory (negligible contact resistance).
additional_findings.source: Moumin et al. 2021, Sec. 2.4 (secondary for Herz 2015 and Wes 1976)
additional_findings.evidence: 'slumping and sliding motions led to an overestimation of the heat transfer coefficient through the models by a factor of 3 and 5'

additional_findings.parameter: Share of covered-wall heat in direct-fired kilns
additional_findings.value: Gorog et al.: wall-to-bed 27 %, 13 % and 7 % of total at gas 790, 1080 and 1650 C. Barr et al.: covered wall 12-25 % of total flux (limestone, refractory kiln). Watkinson-Brimacombe: only 30 % of the gas-to-bed heat by radiation (gas up to 830 C), and better mixing raised gas-to-solid transfer 2-4x. Nafsun 2014: contact transfer up to 20 % in direct-fired kilns and dominant in indirectly heated kilns.
additional_findings.context: For an indirectly (shell) heated pyrolysis drum the covered-wall path dominates, but radiation from the free wall to the bed surface across the freeboard is a parallel path of similar size (see the derived budget).
additional_findings.source: Moumin et al. 2021 Sec. 2.1 (citing Gorog 1982, Barr 1989, Watkinson-Brimacombe 1978); Nafsun et al. 2014 Introduction
additional_findings.evidence: Full-text statements of the citing papers; primaries not opened

additional_findings.parameter: Thermal mixing time in a smooth batch drum (Nafsun et al. 2015)
additional_findings.value: Glass beads 2 mm, F 20 %, 6 rpm: about 59 s (about 6 drum revolutions) to bring bed delta-T <= 5 K. Mixing time falls with rpm and particle size and rises with fill. Revolutions-to-mix rise with rpm (Fig. 8 axis to about 12). Fig. 5-7 values span up to about 600 s at 1 rpm.
additional_findings.context: 0.6 x 0.45 m drum, 1/3/6 rpm, 10/15/20 %, glass beads (lambda 0.25 W/m K, c_p 0.80 kJ/kg K, rho 1.68 g/cm3) and quartz sand (0.10, 1.08, 1.64). Two layers at different temperatures (hot layer about 130 C). Use 3-12 revolutions as the smooth-drum transverse thermal-mixing scale, rather than Wes's 2 revolutions for drums with strips.
additional_findings.source: Nafsun A.I., Herz F., Specht E., Komossa H., Wirtz S., Scherer V., Experimental investigation of thermal bed mixing in rotary drums, HEFAT 2015
additional_findings.evidence: Table 1; Fig. 3/4 text: 'the mixing time for achieve uniform temperature is around 59 seconds'; Figs 5-8 and Conclusions

additional_findings.parameter: Temperature field in a rolling bed is fixed-bed-like away from the active layer
additional_findings.value: Highest temperatures at the wall, lowest in the upper core. Only a thin active layer mixes; the rest moves as a fixed bed. Animal powder (Nafsun): bed temperature decreases with radial distance from the wall.
additional_findings.context: Argues against modelling a rotating bed as perfectly mixed. Resolve the radial profile of the passive layer, or use the penetration/renewal model per contact.
additional_findings.source: Moumin et al. 2021 Sec. 3.4 (Fig. 3.4); Nafsun et al. 2014 (Fig. 4)
additional_findings.evidence: 'This distribution is similar to a fixed bed and was confirmed by visual observation, where only a thin active layer on the top of the bed was seen'

additional_findings.parameter: DERIVED: heat budget of a 10 t batch drum (2.6 x 6.6 m), contact vs radiation
additional_findings.value: Areas at F = 0.67: covered wall 31.7 m2, bed surface 16.5 m2, free wall 22.3 m2 (F = 0.2: 18.1 / 14.9 / 35.8 m2). Heat demand 14-22 GJ (Gamboa 1.41-2.16 kJ/g) to about 30 GJ if sensible heat is added separately. Contact-only at h 25-40 W/m2K and delta-T 200 K: 0.16-0.25 MW (25-50 h). Black-body free-wall-to-bed-surface flux: 21 kW/m2 (600 to 400 C) to 39 kW/m2 (700 to 400 C), i.e. 0.25-0.45 MW at an effective emissivity of about 0.7. Installed burner (Sihai LJ-10) about 1.05 MW.
additional_findings.context: Wall-to-bed-surface radiation is at least as large as covered-wall contact, so both paths must be in the model. Contact alone cannot heat a 10 t charge within the 8-20 h batch times quoted for real plants (Islam 2013: 8 h of firing for 4.5 t).
additional_findings.source: Derived (this verification) from Gamboa et al. 2023, Sihai vendor table and Nafsun 2014
additional_findings.evidence: Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/hv_calc/budget.py

additional_findings.parameter: Vendor fill limit and speed of batch rotary drums
additional_findings.value: Henan Doing: reactor 'left empty 1/3 space to ensure smooth clockwise rotation for 0.4-0.8 r/min', i.e. fill <= 2/3, with a spiral blade inside. Kingtiger: 'Total quantity is controlled to be less than 2/3 of reactor in order to ensure smooth rotation'; maximum reaction temperature about 350 C (vendor); main oil output at 250-280 C (vendor).
additional_findings.context: Batch 'fuel oil + carbon black' drums run at very high fill (up to about 67 %, far outside rolling-bed correlations) and 0.4-0.8 rpm. Carbon black is discharged automatically below 40 C. The Kingtiger/Doing temperatures look like vapour-line or gauge readings and are inconsistent with PE pyrolysis at 400-500 C; treat them as vendor statements, not validation data.
additional_findings.source: Ma J., Zhong Q., Comparison of Chinese pyrolysis processes, WTERT/Columbia (2018), Secs 4.1.2 and 4.2.2
additional_findings.evidence: Quoted text of Step 1 in Secs 4.1.2.1 and 4.2.2.1; Table 5 (Kingtiger BLL-50: reactor 12.5 x 2.2 x 2.5 m, 'Total Power 84 kWh', horizontal and rotary); Table 8 (Doing DY-C-100: 120 kW, Q245R/Q345R, indirect hot-air heating)

additional_findings.parameter: Batch tyre and plastic drum datasheet (Sihai LJ series)
additional_findings.context: Drive motor is 4-11.5 kW, about 0.5 % of burner capacity (3 x 0.35 MW). Vendor marketing data.
additional_findings.source: Sihai Energy Technology, Waste tire/rubber pyrolysis plant product page
additional_findings.evidence: Model and Specification table (Reactor Size, Drive System, Power, Burner rows)

additional_findings.parameter: Beston batch reactors: capacity per batch and reactor life
additional_findings.value: BLJ-16 Standard: whole tyres, sidewall removed, 15-16 t/batch; oil soil 16-18 t/batch; Q345R boiler steel, life 2-3 years. BLJ-16 ULTRA: waste-plastic bales 8-10 t/batch, tyres 15-16 t/batch, 304 stainless, life 5-8 years, ABB explosion-proof motor. BLJ-20: Q345R 2-3 years, 304/316L 5-8 years, 310S 8-10 years. Blackgold P30 (continuous): dynamic seal up to 3 kPa with N2 purge.

additional_findings.source: Beston Group, Tyre pyrolysis plant page (configuration table)
additional_findings.evidence: 'Configuration options' table and 'Upgrade 4: Dynamic Sealing Pressure Capacity Reaching 3 kPa'

additional_findings.parameter: Drive power correlation (CE Raymond / Perry Eq. 20-44) applied to a batch drum
additional_findings.value: bhp = N(4.75 d w + 0.1925 D W + 0.33 W)/1e5 (N rpm; d shell diameter ft; D riding-ring diameter, about d + 2 ft; w live load lb; W total rotating load lb). For 2.6 x 6.6 m, 10 t charge and 25-35 t shell: 3.2-3.4 kW at 0.4 rpm, 6.4-6.7 kW at 0.8 rpm, 8.0-8.4 kW at 1 rpm. The load term is about 80 %. Implied lever arm T/(w d) = 0.249.
additional_findings.context: Compare CoG torque at 2/3 fill: 0.8-1.0 kW at 0.4 rpm. Vendor motors 4-5.5 kW; Metso start-up torque up to 250 % of running torque.
additional_findings.source: NPTEL Chemical Engineering Design II, Module 4 (citing Perry Eq. 20-44); application derived
additional_findings.evidence: Worked example 45.08 bhp = 33.62 kW reproduced; script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/hv_calc/drive.py

additional_findings.parameter: Kiln drive torque sources and start-up (Metso)
additional_findings.value: Resisting torque comes from friction in the carrying and drive mechanisms plus the offset bed at about the angle of repose. Misalignment, seal friction and build-up add to it. Restart with a loaded kiln: up to 250 % of normal running torque. On power loss the offset bed drives the shell backwards, possibly faster than normal forward speed, so a backstop or over-running clutch is fitted. Most kilns run under slight negative pressure, so air infiltrates the seals. Leaf seals and wear bands are replaced every 1-2 years.
additional_findings.context: For a batch pyrolysis drum restarted hot and full (Hedlund 2020: burners fired with the drum NOT rotating), this sets the gearmotor and backstop design and the hazard of a stopped drum.
additional_findings.source: Metso, Rotary kiln handbook, 1st ed. (Dec 2025)
additional_findings.evidence: 'Drive' section p. 21-23; 'Feed and/or discharge housings'; 'Kiln air seal' section

additional_findings.parameter: Seal drag can dominate drive load (PREPP rotary kiln)
additional_findings.value: Original rotary triple seals: excess drag 'overloaded the kiln drive system', and drive motor current rose substantially with kiln temperature. Excess air in-leakage stopped the kiln reaching 980 C (1800 F). Kiln about 8.5 ft x 25 ft at about 0.5 in water (about 125 Pa) negative pressure. Replacement graphite bar seals at 0.03 MPa (5 psi) face pressure.
additional_findings.context: For pyrolysis drums with tight contact seals, budget seal friction torque explicitly; it is not negligible next to the bed torque.
additional_findings.source: OSTI EGG-M--89466, PREPP rotary kiln seals - problem and resolution
additional_findings.evidence: Abstract and sections 'Evaluation of problem' and 'Replacement seal'

additional_findings.parameter: NFPA 69 (F2023 draft) updated LOC values, N2-air
additional_findings.context: Pyrolysis gas contains H2 (LOC < 5 %), so under 7.7.2.5(2) a monitored system must stay <= 0.6 x 4.6 = 2.76 vol% O2, and an unmonitored one <= 1.84 vol%. Hedlund cites a pyrolysis-gas LOC at 520 C possibly as low as 3 vol% (Cuypers 2011). The O2 <= 1 % patent target meets both.
additional_findings.source: NFPA 69 First Draft Report (F2023 cycle), Annex Table C.1(a)
additional_findings.evidence: Table C.1(a) 'Limiting Oxidant Concentrations for Flammable Gases When Nitrogen or Carbon Dioxide Are Used as Diluents', 'Updated or (Adjusted) Data' vs 'Original Data' columns; footnote a = 120 L apparatus (Zlochower and Green)

additional_findings.parameter: P4O batch rotary-kiln plastic pyrolysis reactor (Hedlund 2023)
additional_findings.value: Rotary kiln 10 m long, about 2.5 m diameter. Oil/gas burners in a combustion chamber below, flue-gas jacket, hinged bolted endcap for forklift loading of baled plastic. PSV set below 50 kPa (to stay outside the EU PED). Light and heavy oil condensed; NCG partly flared. 2021 charge: 7 t of baled plastic. Explosion 30 min after burner light-off. 40 kPa N2 pressurisation of an air-filled vessel leaves 15 vol% O2.
additional_findings.context: A real batch 'plastic to oil' drum of the size class the event model targets. It is the documented static-heating hazard: burners fired with the drum not rotating, and the wall above the gas AIT.
additional_findings.source: Hedlund F.H., Chem. Eng. Trans. 99 (2023) 241-246, doi:10.3303/CET2399041
additional_findings.evidence: Sections 'Plant' (p. 243), 'Explosion 2020', 'Explosion 2021' and 'Discussion' (p. 245-246)

additional_findings.parameter: Rotary-kiln tyre pyrolysis yields vs temperature (pilot)
additional_findings.value: Galvagno et al. pilot rotary kiln, 550 to 680 C: char 49.09 to 48.86 wt%, oil 38.12 to 31.82 wt%, gas 2.39 to 10.75 wt%. Yazdani et al. (N2, 400-1050 C): maximum oil 44 wt% at 550 C; higher temperature means more gas and less char.
additional_findings.context: Use instead of the unsupported '15/40/45 +/-' figures. The review also notes that rotary kilns suffer uneven temperature distribution, high heat loss, and char with more volatiles, ash and sulfur from incomplete pyrolysis.

additional_findings.value: Per 10 t batch: diesel about 300 kg, or pyrolysis oil 300-400 kg, or CNG about 150 m3, or LPG 100-150 kg, or wood about 700-800 kg, or coal about 500 kg. Average electrical power about 30 kW for about 10 h (about 300 kWh/day). 10 t of tyres gives an average 4.5 t of oil.

additional_findings.value: Idle 3.11 kW; 3.22 kW at 470 kg/h (hold-up ratio 57 %); 3.46 kW at 320 kg/h (comparative example). Load share 0.11-0.35 kW.

verdict_fulltext.summary:
Network this time: the DLR, UPSpace (Univ. Pretoria), OSTI, NFPA, Metso, NPTEL, cetjournal, ache-pub, UNAL, Porto repository, WTERT, Wikipedia, FEECO, Google Patents (intermittent) and the vendor sites (china-doing, Sihai, Beston, wastetireoil) were readable. Blocked or challenged: ScienceDirect, ACS, MDPI and ResearchGate (403); core.ac.uk PDFs and link.springer.com (JS/Cloudflare challenge); the Halle/Magdeburg repository (Anubis bot wall, not bypassed); umpir.ump.edu.my (DNS); patents.justia (403); Scribd, SlideShare and pdfcoffee. So Herz 2012 (IJHMT/CES), Nafsun 2017/2018, Emady, Figueroa, Chaudhuri, Liu 2016 and Wu 2019 remain unverifiable.

Confirmed in full text:
- Penetration HTC and contact time t = gamma*60/(2*pi*n) (Moumin 2021, Eqs 2.3 and 2.4; gamma is the full angle, n in rpm). The formula reproduces Nafsun 2014's 'Wes' column within 1-3 %.
- Moumin's cohesive-powder result: models over-predict 2.5-6x; strips add 2.2-3.1x.
- Durdevic 2024; US 11,987,756; US 5,167,772.
- US 9,777,159: O2 <= 1 % and +/-3 in WC. Note it is a vertical tray reactor, not a kiln.
- PREPP seal data; NFPA 69 margin clauses; Wikipedia 800 kW; Metso 250 % start torque; FEECO drive limits.
- US 9,683,779 drive power; Ma & Zhong yields; Doing fuel and electricity FAQ; Yanez LDPE melt alpha.
- Islam 2013 and Gamboa 2023 from abstracts only.

Corrected:
1. Hedlund: Danish plant (Egebjerg); batch rotary kiln 10 m x 2.5 m; 7 t of baled plastic; 40 kPa N2 leaves 15 % O2.
2. LOC: NFPA 69 updated N2 values are H2 4.6, CO 5.1, CH4 11.1, C2H4 8.5, C3H8 10.7. The monitored O2 limit is therefore 2.76 %, not about 3 %.
3. FEECO double leaf is '<<1-3 %'; the '25 % of single leaf' wording is not on the page.
4. Doing DY-1-10 condenser area is 100 m2, not 40. The 19 kW is on Doing's own page (a reseller says 15 kW). Batch-time details were not seen.
5. Sihai drive table corrected; Huayin power is 'average 15 kW'.
6. The 'sqrt(n) straight lines' claim is wrong. Measured h(6)/h(1) is only 1.2-2.4.
7. The Porto '15/40/45 +/-' yields are not in the cited review.
8. The rotating-bed h_pen of 47-93 W/m2K over-predicts. Measured analogues (expanded clay: 27-41 W/m2K at 1 rpm, 36-54 at 6 rpm, F 20 %) point to 20-40 W/m2K for plastic-like beds before melting.
9. Static-time and torque corrections from the earlier verifier upheld.

Key additions for the model:
- Measured h_ws table for six materials (Nafsun 2014) as a validation set.
- Full correlation constants (Tscheng-Watkinson 11.6 and 0.3; chi 0.085 and 0.1; Schlunder-Mollekopf terms).
- A rolling bed is fixed-bed-like outside a thin active layer; smooth-drum thermal mixing takes about 6 revolutions (59 s at 6 rpm), not 2.
- Batch drums run at up to 2/3 fill and 0.4-0.8 rpm (Doing, Kingtiger).
- CE Raymond/Perry drive formula checked via NPTEL (D = riding-ring diameter, linear). It gives 3.2-3.4 kW at 0.4 rpm for a 10 t drum; three industrial rules imply a lever arm of about 0.25 D.
- Heat budget: free-wall-to-bed radiation (0.25-0.45 MW) is at least as large as covered-wall contact (0.16-0.25 MW) in a 10 t drum, so both paths are needed.

verify:designs+valid.summary:
I checked threads A (designs) and F (validation) against the full texts I could reach: about 44 tool calls, 33 items. The verdicts are 14 confirmed, 11 corrected and 8 unverifiable, with no outright refutations. Two items carry a probable-misattribution flag, and several open copies were behind bot walls that I did not try to get past.

**Confirmed from full text**
- **DGE Hamm kiln:** D 2.8 m, heated L 20 m, about 15% fill, about 90 min, about 500 °C process, about 750 °C shell, 6.65 t/h per kiln. The data sheet also gives a full mass and energy balance; from it I derived a gross firing of about 2.2 MJ per kg of feed and about 1.5 MJ/kg net to the process.
- **Suzuki 2008 heat-transfer coefficients:** 38.6 / 45.3 / 50.1 W/m2K, and 22 to 55 W/m2K at a 555 °C wall.
- **Zhou 2025 medical-waste kiln (abstract only):** all its heat-transfer numbers.
- **Westerhout 1997 HDPE kinetics:** k0 = 1.9e13 s^-1 and Ea = 220 kJ/mol (Table 4), valid only up to 450 °C. The derived times to 90% conversion (t90) are 15.7 min at 450 °C and 1.48 min at 500 °C (extrapolated).
- **Other full-text checks:** the heat-loss fractions and kiln size from Qasim 2025, the Pichler simulation dataset design, the Bhatt kiln geometry, the Ma & Zhong survey of Chinese plants, and the US 11319493 patent (20 cm x 230 cm insert, vapour residence cut by nearly half).
- **Sullivan residence-time formula:** T = 1.77·A^0.5·L·FACTOR/(S·D·N), with FACTOR = 1 for a plain kiln. This comes from an EPA appendix that cites the Allis Mineral Systems model, so it is secondary rather than the 1927 original.
- **Arithmetic:** the bed-geometry, Froude-number and residence-time calculations are correct.

**Corrections**
1. **Suzuki: two papers, not one.** The 22–55 W/m2K values are from JTST 3:523 and the lifter values are from JTST 3:532. The kiln is batch, 1 m ID x 1.5 m, fed with simulated waste that is only 35% plastic. Speed alone (2.7 to 4.0 rpm) gives 38.6 to 43.4 W/m2K. The 50.1 W/m2K needs both 4.0 rpm and six 200 mm lifters.
2. **Suzuki: definitions.** The coefficient is per unit of internal wall area, not covered area. The paper contradicts itself on the lifter-spacing rule: the abstract says spacing ratio > 1, Section 3.3 says < 1.
3. **Kodera 2021.** The abstract says only "2-kg/h plant", not "1 to 3 kg/h". Only the annual fuel-gas figures (3.86e7 / 1.49e7 / 2.42e7 MJ/y) and the USD 2,467,000 break-even appear there. The bench and 200 kg/h geometry and the gas yields remain unverified because ScienceDirect blocks the full text.
4. **Zhang 2020.** The abstract confirms the 15% heat-carrier optimum and 89.1% gasoline-range content. "57.6 wt% oil at 625 °C" is not in it, and a search found no source. The "1/3/6 rpm, 10/15/20% fill, one of four models" test matrix matches Herz et al. 2012, so it is probably misattributed.
5. **Kern 2012 straw pilot.** The 67% chemical efficiency is for DDGS; straw is 0.55.
6. **Mines Albi pilot kiln.** Maximum temperature is 1050 °C, not 1000 °C.
7. **Moumin 2021.** The second material is cement raw meal, not petroleum coke. It also gives a usable sand target: 136.5 W/m2K at 10% fill and 1 rpm.
8. **Jaworski 2023.** The rig ran at 1, 1.5 and 2 rpm and 1–3° slope. The quoted 0.25–4.5 rpm is a generic industrial range.
9. **Westerhout PS constants.** 3.3e13 s^-1 / 204 kJ/mol is the first-order fit. The RCD-model fit is 1.3e14 s^-1 / 219 kJ/mol.
10. **Li et al. 2005 contact model.** The constant χ is documented as 0.1 (and 0.085 for Sullivan & Sabersky). The claimed 0.096–0.198 range was not seen.
11. **Tscheng–Watkinson correlation.** The constant 11.6 and exponent 0.3 are right, but the rotation term is angular velocity ω in rad/s, not rev/s.

**Still unverifiable**
- **Froude-number regime limits:** the Mellmann and Henein limits; the Henein PDF returned 403 and SciELO is behind a challenge.
- **Correlations and inert-bed datasets:** Specht's discharge-end correlation (F0 = 1.75·Bd^0.5) and the Barr T4 / Tscheng A11 data. The Hanein manuscript is behind a Cloudflare challenge.
- **Liu/Dai/Li 2026 HDPE gas yields:** the paper exists (J. Environ. Chem. Eng. 14:122678, doi 10.1016/j.jece.2026.122678), but the numbers are unseen.
- **Two Chinese-journal claims:** the 4 r/min optimum and the 5% heat-carrier slipping result.
- **Li A.M. 1999 snippet numbers:** the abstract has trends only.
- **Bed-depth equation (Saeman/Kramers–Croockewit):** the two threads agree algebraically, but neither form was checked against a primary source. Note that the usual published form has an extra 1/cos(β) factor.

PMC, HAL, aidic.it, the Henein page and the Aberdeen repository all returned anti-bot pages or errors, and I did not bypass them. I read the PMC papers through the official Europe PMC API instead. Downloaded files are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/vAF (Suzuki s_3_3_523.txt and s_3_3_532.txt, hamm.txt, wester.txt, moumin.txt, kern.txt, qasim.txt, wtert.txt, pat.txt, and the PMC texts).

verify:bed+heat.summary:
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION OF THREADS B (bed mechanics) AND C (heat transfer), about 40 tool calls. Thread C was checked against the full texts already in the scratchpad: Nafsun, Colin, Hared, Patisson, Thammavong, Lebas, Beckmann, the Herz brochure, CIESC and Ma. The two Suzuki J-STAGE PDFs were downloaded again and read. I recomputed the derived numbers independently in scratchpad/vBCs/chk.py.

THREAD C. Most decision-critical numbers are CONFIRMED exactly:
- Nafsun Tables 1 and 2: all 6 materials x 2 rpm x 5 columns.
- Suzuki 2008: k_m-w 22 to 55 W/m2K at a 555 °C wall and 27 to 55 at 630 °C; flux 11 and 16.5 kW/m2; SUS310S geometry; waste recipe.
- Lifter data: 38.6 / 45.3 / 50.1 W/m2K.
- Li chi 0.096-0.198 and Colin's chi(dp) fit.
- Tscheng gas Nu exponents 0.575, 0.535, 0.104, 0.292 and 0.341 (Colin's gas-wall 0.535 is a typo).
- Gorog 0.036 Re^0.8; Seghir-Ouali.
- L_m = 0.95 (D - H); the 20 % gray-gas bound; Manitius within 5 %.
- Emissivities 0.87-0.91 (347 SS) and 0.9.
- Regenerative wall: 15 mm and 75 °C. Outside coefficients 0.26 / 3-40 / 17.
- Beckmann PE pilot conditions. All derived HTC arithmetic.

CORRECTIONS (thread C):
1. Lifters alone raise k_m-w by 17 % (38.6 to 45.3). The +30 % needs lifters plus 4 rpm.
2. Colin's chi fit gives 2.35 at 4 mm, not 0.59, and it must not be extrapolated beyond 2 mm.
3. The Tscheng wall-bed argument differs between sources by 2 pi to 4 pi^2, not by 2, because Patisson Eq. 20 contains pi and an angular velocity. That is a factor of 1.7-3 in h, and the units of n in the original are still unknown.
4. The CIESC abstract also reports that 3 r/min INHIBITED heat transfer at the low heating rate in the drying and pre-pyrolysis stages. This is a caveat for the KINTEK claim.
5. Beckmann's '4.600 kJ/kg' is ambiguous (4600 or 4.6) and fits neither reading of PE DSC data, so do not use it.

Unverifiable: the patent value 74-107, melt and flake-bed conductivity, and the molten-film HTC.

THREAD B. This thread was built from snippets and memory, so it was the weaker one.
Confirmed:
- The Fr definition, and the rolling band 1e-4 < Fr < 1e-2 attributed to Mellmann, via the Santos 2016 BJCE full text. Henein's band is 5e-4 to 2e-2.
- Sullivan 1.77 L sqrt(theta)/(D S n), in Colin Eq. 6 and the Rutgers thesis. Spread: Rutgers uses the static angle; Lebas implies a coefficient of about 1.47.
- The Saeman ODE form, against Patisson Eq. 1, and the worked example (17.6 / 22.1 / 29.8 min).
- The Sullivan = shallow-Saeman check, the fill geometry and contact times, the Fr examples, the Rayleigh DEM time steps and the drag-out film formula.

Corrected:
- The '38 % fill' case is about 28 % at normal depth (20 % mean).
- The operating window per the open sources is 1-3° slope, 1-5 rpm (Colin, citing Boateng) and 10-20 % fill (Nafsun).
- Pe is NOT about 10^2. Measured values are 361-645 (Colin 2015, wood chips) and about 2000 (Thammavong, L/D 19). So plug flow plus a Pe sensitivity of 300-2000 is the right setting.
- Angle of repose: the analogues are PP spheres at 30-35° (in a PP/glass mixture) and flake-like wood chips at 42°.

Unverifiable (originals closed, CLOSED per Semantic Scholar or anti-bot pages): the full Mellmann Table 1 (slumping, cascading, slipping and cataracting bands and the f conditions), Henein's boundary values, Ding's group, active-layer delta/h, and the polymer Tm values.

KEY NEW VALIDATION DATASET: Colin et al. 2015 Table 2 gives 8 runs with slope, rpm, feed, hold-up, MRT, sigma, J, Pe and D_ax for a 0.21 x 4.2 m kiln with 42° chips. On it, Sullivan is within ±13 %, and the plain Saeman ODE overpredicts MRT by 4-25 % and hold-up somewhat. This is a direct benchmark for the kiln's axial-transport module.

verdicts.parameter: [D] Bhatt et al. 2026 semi-pilot rotary kiln: mixed plastics 43 wt% oil and 16 wt% char at 500 °C

Gas is computed by difference (100 - oil - char) and so includes losses: about 41 wt% using the abstract values. The authors state that gas composition could not be determined. Kiln details missing from the thread: SS304 drum 1360 mm long, OD 355 mm, wall 3 mm, N2 5 L/min. The mixed-plastic feed was mostly LDPE + PP, with PS and HDPE below 2%. verdicts.parameter: [D] Pohl et al. 2026 (KIT): gas composition against temperature for HDPE/PP
verdicts.claimed: At 700 and 800 °C ethylene is the main product, then methane, with acetylene at 900-1500 °C; H2 12.8 wt% at 1600 °C; HDPE has about 14.2 wt% H; residence 10 s at 1 bar, Ar
verdicts.corrected_value: For HDPE the claims hold: ethylene is the primary product at 700-800 °C and peaks around 800-900 °C; methane dominates at 900-1200 °C; C2H2 matters at 900-1500 °C; ethane and propylene become negligible at 1000 °C and above. 12.8 wt% H2 corresponds to about 90.1% of the H. PP behaves differently: it gives less ethylene and significant propylene at 800 °C (undetectable above 1000 °C), and methane dominates at lower temperatures, peaking at about 1000-1200 °C. The 'ethylene first' statement therefore applies to HDPE only.
verdicts.source_checked: Pohl et al., React. Chem. Eng. 2026 (KITopen full text, local kit190723.txt), Figs. 2 and 4-5 text
verdicts.note: Argon flow is 175 mL/min for τ = 10 s; 0.3 g per run. The 14.2 wt% H is quoted from He et al.; the stoichiometric H content of (CH2)n is 14.4 wt%.

verdicts.parameter: [D] PVC two-stage kinetics (Polymers 2021, PMC8706959)
verdicts.claimed: Stage I 75 kJ/mol, A 1.81e6 min-1, P2 (490-675 K); stage II 140 kJ/mol, A 4.84e9 min-1, F3 (675-825 K); literature: 48.6/48.1/49.8 (FWO/KAS/Friedman) and 190/250 kJ/mol; HCl 58.3 wt%
verdicts.corrected_value: The abstract gives 1.81e6 min-1 for stage I (isoconversional average), but the final rate equation in the kinetic table uses A1 = 1.79e6 min-1: dα/dt = 1.79e6 exp(-75000/RT)·2α^(1/2). Stage II: 4.84e9 exp(-140000/RT)(1-α)^3. In s-1 these are 2.98e4 and 8.07e7. Literature pairs: 190 kJ/mol (A 4.40e7 min-1, n 1.5) and 250 kJ/mol (A 6.57e7 min-1, n 1.6). Authors: Al-Yaari M. and Dubdub I. TGA residue at 825 K is about 20 wt%, against 5-6 wt% fixed carbon in proximate analysis.
verdicts.source_checked: PMC8706959 abstract, sections 3.1-3.2 and kinetic table (full text, local copy)
verdicts.note: For a CFD solver, P2 f(α) = 2α^(1/2) gives zero rate at α = 0, so seed α0 of about 1e-4 or start from a nucleation step. The HCl stoichiometry 36.46/62.50 = 0.583 is correct. The model-fit Ea (P2 79, F3 125 kJ/mol) differ slightly from the isoconversional averages.

verdicts.parameter: [E] van Wyk 2026 cited by Li 2026: '<30% compositional change at 750 °C in 4 s', used to neglect gas-phase reactions

verdicts.corrected_value: The quote in Li et al. is confirmed, but it does not mean primary vapours survive at 750 °C. Van Wyk et al. (Fuel 407, 2026, 137561) ran a steam (S/C 0.8) bubbling fluidized bed at 750 °C, sampling at 1.6 / 4.4 / 8.2 s (PE, PP) and 1.6 / 4.6 / 8.6 s (DKR-350). At 1.6 s the product is already a light gas rich in CH4, C2H4 and C3H6, with benzene/toluene and tar. C3H6 then falls 37-47% within 3 s, while C2H4 stays roughly stable for PE. The '<30% change' describes the already-cracked light-gas slate. It supports fast wax/oil cracking at 750 °C, not negligible cracking.
verdicts.source_checked: Li et al., Particuology 115 (2026), section 2.1 (local kitfb.txt); van Wyk et al. 2026 TNO open copy (abstract, sections 2-3)

Pilot tubular reactor at about 400-460 °C.

additional_findings.parameter: van Wyk et al. 2026: secondary cracking of polyolefin vapours at 750 °C against gas residence time
additional_findings.value: Bubbling fluidized bed at 750 °C, steam-to-carbon 0.8. Freeboard ID 102 mm × 600 mm; sampling at 1.6 / 4.4 / 8.2 s (PE, PP) and 1.6 / 4.6 / 8.6 s (DKR-350). Product gas is rich in CH4, C2H4 and C3H6 already at 1.6 s. C3H6 falls 37-47% within 3 s; C2H4 is roughly stable for PE and rises for PP; CH4 and H2 rise with time. For PP, benzene + toluene is 21-22 m/m% and tar 14 m/m%; the other feeds give about 11-12 m/m% tar. The largest change occurs between 1.6 and 5 s.
additional_findings.context: Wall-side or high-T anchor for freeboard cracking. Primary wax/oil vapour is essentially fully converted to light gases within 1.6 s at 750 °C. This is consistent with Option B (k_O about 4.8 s-1 at 750 °C) and does not support neglecting gas-phase chemistry in a hot kiln freeboard.
additional_findings.source: van Wyk S., Mourao Vilela C.F., Meijwes C., Geusebroek M., Toonen A., 'Thermal cracking of polyolefin waste: primary and secondary product formation as a function of gas phase residence time in bubbling fluidized bed', Fuel 407 (2026) 137561
additional_findings.evidence: Abstract: 'Product gases were simultaneously measured at three different heights above the fluidized bed, corresponding to residence times of 1.6–10 s ... C3H6 ... decreasing significantly (37–47 % within three seconds)'

additional_findings.parameter: Pires 2025 short-cut rate fits (thermal HDPE, first stage)
additional_findings.value: Rg = 1.63 exp(-3539.68/T); Rl = 3.40 exp(-4068.03/T); Rl+ = 267.94 exp(-5889.43/T), as mass fraction produced per minute (R = M·phi/Δt)
additional_findings.context: Zero-order-like rates fitted to the three 30-min runs at 450/500/550 °C. They are the basis of the '73 min to full conversion at 450 °C' statement. Use them only as an empirical validation curve, not as kinetics.

additional_findings.evidence: 'Rg = 1.63 exp(−3539.68/TR)'; 'at 450 °C ... a residence time of 73 minutes might be required to convert the plastic feed into products'

additional_findings.parameter: Pires 2025 catalytic HDPE yields (Y zeolite Cat1 and Cat2, 1:1 catalyst:polymer, 30 min)
additional_findings.context: Contrast case only. The thermal-only kiln baseline is in Table 3.3. Errors are ± 3.86 (liquid), 3.73 (gas), 0.44 (solid) and 1.17 (coke).
additional_findings.source: Pires 2025, Tables 3.3-3.4
additional_findings.evidence: Table 3.3 rows C1_450-C2_550 read directly

additional_findings.parameter: Bhatt et al. 2026 rotary kiln (paper/biomass co-pyrolysis): temperature series
additional_findings.value: 2 kg batch, preheated at 150 °C for 1 h, ramped at 20 °C/min to 450 / 550 / 650 °C, 90 min hold, 1 rpm. Oil yield about 31% at 450 °C and about 45% at 650 °C; char about 48% at 450 °C and 24% at 650 °C. Co-pyrolysis maximum 48 wt% oil with 20 wt% char at 650 °C; oil HHV 39-43 MJ/kg.

additional_findings.parameter: Bhatt et al. 2026 kiln geometry and operation (PMC13329883)
additional_findings.value: SS304 horizontal drum, 1360 mm long, OD 355 mm, wall 3 mm. N2 5 L/min; 2 rpm; 20 °C/min to 500 °C, 90 min. Primary oil vessel at 200 °C (2 kW heater) followed by 3 water-cooled shell-and-tube condensers in series (water 25-30 °C in, 35-50 °C out). Gas yield = 100 - oil - char.
additional_findings.context: A small-kiln validation geometry with a measured operating point. The char yield is inconsistent between abstract (16 wt%) and results (5-7 wt% for pure plastics).
additional_findings.source: Bhatt M. et al., RSC Adv. (2026), PMC13329883, section 2.5
additional_findings.evidence: 'made of stainless steel 304, 1360 mm long, with an O.D. of 355 mm and a wall thickness of 3 mm'; 'maintained at 5 L min−1'; 'operated at 2 rpm and maintained at 500 °C'

additional_findings.value: 2 kilns × 6.65 t/h (13 t/h plant, 100,000 t/a); availability 85%. At 100% load: natural gas 800 Nm3/h (Hu 36,000 kJ/Nm3, about 8.0 MW), electricity 700 kW, N2 20 m3/h, compressed air 10 m3/h. Feed Cl 0.1-3.0 wt%; S 0.01-2.0 wt%.

additional_findings.source: DGEngineering, Hamm MW Pyrolysis Plant (July 2009)

additional_findings.parameter: Recomputed vapour residence time per Hamm kiln
additional_findings.value: 64 s (M = 50 g/mol), 191 s (M = 150), 383 s (M = 300), from outlet-flow V/Q
additional_findings.context: Assumptions: 6.65 t/h, 70% volatiles, 500 °C, 1 atm, 104.7 m3 free volume (85% of π/4·2.8²·20). Replaces the thread D estimate of 20-35 s.
additional_findings.source: Derived here from the Hamm data sheet
additional_findings.evidence: Python: n = 6.65e3/3600·0.7/M; Q = nRT/p; τ = V/Q

additional_findings.parameter: Li et al. 2026 simulation matrix and temperature sensitivity
additional_findings.value: Batch cases at TR 505 / 515 / 525 °C need gas inlet 540 / 550 / 561 °C. Particle size 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 mm. Continuous case feeds 0.0234 g/s with gas inlet 624 °C and sand initially at 500 °C. LF yield falls from 67.4 to 56.7 wt% and G rises from 29.6 to 40.9 wt% as TR goes from 505 to 525 °C; HF is about 3 wt% throughout.
additional_findings.context: Shows how sharply a 20 K bed-temperature change moves the oil/gas split with this lumped scheme. Useful for presenting kiln wall-temperature sensitivity.
additional_findings.source: Li M. et al., Particuology 115 (2026) 214-227, Table 4 and section 4.2.1
additional_findings.evidence: 'With increasing TR, LF yield decreases (from 67.4 to 56.7 wt%), while G production increases (from 29.6 to 40.9 wt%)'

additional_findings.parameter: PVC rate laws as used in code (Al-Yaari & Dubdub 2021)
additional_findings.value: Stage I: dα/dt = 1.79e6 exp(-75000/RT)·2α^(1/2) [min-1], or 2.98e4 s-1. Stage II: dα/dt = 4.84e9 exp(-140000/RT)(1-α)^3 [min-1], or 8.07e7 s-1. About 20 wt% residue at 825 K in TGA.
additional_findings.context: P2 needs a nonzero seed conversion. The abstract quotes A1 = 1.81e6 min-1 (isoconversional average). The TGA residue (about 20 wt%) is much higher than the proximate fixed carbon (5-6 wt%).
additional_findings.source: Pyrolytic Behavior of PVC, Polymers 13 (2021), PMC8706959, kinetic table and section 3.1

additional_findings.parameter: Kinetic vs observed conversion in 30 min at 450 °C (HDPE)
additional_findings.value: 98.8% (Westerhout first order, k = 2.44e-3 s-1) and 99.5% (RS-L2 set) predicted, against about 20% measured (80.09 ± 0.22 wt% solid left)
additional_findings.context: A direct demonstration of heat-up and heat-transfer limits in real reactors, and a strong argument for coupling bed heat transfer to the kinetics in the kiln model. Pires' sample heat-up history is not reported.
additional_findings.source: Calculated here from Westerhout 1997 Table 4 and Pires 2025 Table 3.3

additional_findings.value: In the drop-tube setup the polymer decomposition temperature does not exceed 550 °C even at 900 °C ambient. Literature: PE stays below 600 °C for Text > 900 °C.
additional_findings.context: Supports a bed held near 450-550 °C under a 700-750 °C kiln shell (Hamm: 500 °C process, 750 °C shell).
additional_findings.source: Locaspi et al., Proc. Combust. Inst. 41 (2025) 105912, section 4

verify:chem+model.summary:
I checked both threads against the full texts already downloaded to the scratchpad (vAF, tD2, topicE) and fetched a few more. New work is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Programacao/381db60a-cc64-54cc-aefe-1e483b5b217d/scratchpad/vDE (chk.py recomputes every derived number).

THREAD D (chemistry). Most decision-critical numbers hold.
- Westerhout 1997 Tables 4-6 and the additive-mixture result are confirmed digit for digit.
- Lechleitner kLit and the 460 °C rates are confirmed.
- Pires Tables 3.3 and 3.4 are confirmed.
- Locaspi 2025 is confirmed: mechanism size, k = 0.8e16 exp(-71000/RT) with units inferred, ethylene at most 40-50 wt%, and the wet-bulb limit.
- The PVC Ea and A values, the WTERT vendor claims and all t90 and energy arithmetic are confirmed.

Corrections and refutations in thread D:
1. Jaworski's '610 kg/m3 plastic pellets' is wrong. That pellet is a biomass pellet (20 × 6 mm) used in a cold-flow incineration-kiln model.
2. Hamm runs two kilns at 6.65 t/h each, so the 20-35 s vapour residence time becomes about 1-6 min (64 s at M = 50 g/mol, 190-380 s for waxy vapour), in line with thread E.
3. The Lechleitner k1..k6 path map can be read from Eqs. 2-6: k1 W->SO, k2 W->LL, k3 W->G, k4 SO->LL, k5 SO->G, k6 LL->G. Hr '73,289' is 73.3 kJ/mol written with a decimal comma.
4. Pires' 73 min is a zero-order short-cut extrapolation, not a measurement. The real contrast is 20% measured conversion in 30 min at 450 °C against 98.8% from Westerhout first-order kinetics. Table 3.4 is internally inconsistent: at 500 °C the carbon cuts sum to 104.7%.
5. Bhatt's rotary-kiln paper contradicts itself on char: 16 wt% in the abstract, 5-7 wt% in the results. Its gas yield is by difference.
6. In Pohl 2026, 'ethylene first at 700-800 °C' applies to HDPE only. PP gives methane and propylene.
7. In the PVC final rate law A1 = 1.79e6 min-1, not the abstract's 1.81e6. P2 needs a seed conversion.
8. Locaspi Eq. 1 includes ρL, and its convective term is explicit.

Still unverifiable: Stoliarov DSC heats (FAA server 503, journal closed) and the Aboulkas Ea (abstract withheld). The RS-L2 E values therefore remain abstract-level.

THREAD E (gas phase and modelling). Confirmed in full text:
- Lund/Star-CCM+ setup and cost table (21.6/32.5/46.2 h for 15 s) and the 540 vs 600 K gap.
- Abdy residence times and wax yields.
- Li 2026 five-lump Table 2 (ΔH 542 kJ/kg on the wax steps, 0 on PP->W) and the about one day per few seconds 3D cost.
- Barr's <30% and 15-55 W/m2K, Boateng Table 4.2 for PE pellets (all endpoints).
- Le Guen coefficients and correlation constants, Chaudhuri calciner data and the Hc law, Chrono::GPU regimes and throughput, T4 specs, and all derived freeboard numbers.

Corrections in thread E:
1. Barr's 2-3 W/m2K convection at Re = 2000 is Watkinson & Brimacombe's result, reviewed in Barr's thesis.
2. Le Guen's nominal hbg (102.83) already sits outside its stated 50-100 validity range. The hsw correlation is valid only for ω = 3.5-10 rad/s, so real kilns are an extrapolation.
3. Lechleitner should be cited as 2021.

Most important cross-thread finding: van Wyk et al. 2026, which Li et al. cite as '<30% change at 750 °C in 4 s' to neglect gas-phase reactions, was read in full. At 750 °C the vapour is already light gas (CH4, C2H4, C3H6, plus benzene/toluene and tar) by 1.6 s, and C3H6 then falls 37-47% within 3 s. The citation does not justify neglecting freeboard cracking. Instead it supports the fast high-temperature cracking of thread D's Option B (k_O about 4.8 s-1 at 750 °C).

Option B values recomputed: 5.4e-5 / 9.2e-4 / 0.0113 / 0.106 / 0.79 s-1 at 500-700 °C. Oil conversion is 4.9% at 625 °C / 1.4 s and 81% at 675 °C / 5.6 s (Gracida-Alvarez anchor); Option A gives 27% at 550 °C / 96 s. Option B stays our own calibration and should be presented as such.
